jobs.title: EHV EPC Project Manager (Power Delivery)- Remote
jobs.description:
Job Description

WSP is seeking EHV EPC Project Manager (Power Delivery)- Remote
for our Power & Energy Program Management Office in Portland, OR.
The following locations will also be considered: Los Angeles, CA, San Francisco, CA, San Diego, CA, Seattle, WA, Boise, ID, Helena, MT and Phoenix, AZ.
In this position, you will be responsible for cradle-to-grave execution of high-voltage transmission EPC projects, from project development and design through construction, energization, and final closeout.

This Opportunity

This position provides high level technical project leadership, and guidance with managing the administrative, commercial, and technical components of EHV Transmission and Substation project(s) or portfolio of projects in accordance with WSP’s core values, and the level of project services agreed upon in the contract by WSP and the client(s).

Responsible for the overall performance of assigned project(s) that are moderate and larger size/complexity and regional in scope, and includes oversight for financial, technical, client satisfaction, quality, safety, and schedule.

Ensures that responsibilities throughout the project lifecycle (proposal phase, project startup and planning, project execution, reporting, and project closeout) are adhered to, delivered, and audited with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable corporate standards for safety, execution, profitability, and operational purpose.

Your Impact

Coordinate and communicate with all levels of management and disciplines throughout the project life cycle to support project cost and schedule objectives, both internally and within the client’s systems.
Lead the development of project proposals, cost estimates, scope, schedules, and resource plans
Oversee management of budgeting, forecasting, scheduling, cost and change management and control.
Provide regular project reporting and updates to clients, technical leads, and business leaders, identifying any emergent issues with scope, risk, and/or budget and mitigation strategies.
Be the face of WSP for the client. Develop and nurture strong, long-term relationships with client by understanding their needs, providing tailored solutions, and ensuring consistent communication to drive satisfaction and retention.
Adherence to proven processes and ability to develop new processes to standardize procedures.
Adhere to safety regulations and enforce project safety standards
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree (Electrical, Civil, Mechanical, Project Management or Construction Management), Engineering Technology, Physical Sciences, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience within an A/E/C firm, utility, EPC, or power delivery consulting environment.
10+ years of relevant post education experience in a project management role within our industry.
3+ years of EHV transmission level voltage project experience (115kV up to 500kV)
Cradle to grave EPC project management experience for transmission level voltage
Highly proficient understanding of project delivery process and strong background and experience in project management. Experience managing projects through a variety of delivery models (DBB, EPC, PDB).
Advanced proficiency with analytical and organizational skills, with business acumen to bridge the business and project management.
Advanced proficiency with interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively, persuasively, and tactfully with leadership, subcontractors, and employees at all levels of the organization.
Excellent self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and adjusting readily to the changing prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
Works independently and provides guidance and leadership to mid-level to senior level team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
Advanced proficiency with technical writing, office automation, relevant software, MS Office suite products (e.g., Word, Excel, Visio, Project, SharePoint), technology, spreadsheets, and PM tools.
Ability to elicit cooperation from a wide variety of sources, including senior management, subcontractors, consultants, and company-wide staff, including those with whom no formal hierarchical relationship exits.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Strong ability to quickly adapt to change and demonstrate flexibility to a variety of schedules and hours to meet project-specific needs.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.

WSP Benefits

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation

Expected Salary (all locations): $120,000 - $210,000

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

WSP provides a flexible and agile workplace model while meeting client needs. Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

WSP USA (and all of its U.S. companies) is an Equal Opportunity Employer Race/Age/Color/Religion/Sex/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity/National Origin/Disability or Protected Veteran Status.

The selected candidate must be authorized to work in the United States.

Notice To Third Party Agencies

WSP does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters, employment agencies, or other staffing services. Unsolicited resumes include any resume or hiring document sent to WSP in the absence of a signed Service Agreement where WSP has expressly requested recruitment/staffing services specific to the position at hand. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers or other business leaders, will become the property of WSP and WSP will have the right to hire that candidate without reservation – no fee or other compensation will be owed or paid to the recruiter, employment agency, or other staffing service.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Electrical Commissioning
jobs.description:
Company Description

A subsidiary of Veolia group, Veolia North America (VNA) is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country's largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. VNA helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education, and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Mass., Veolia North America has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across the continent.

www.veolianorthamerica.com

Job Description

Veolia (formerly SourceOne Inc.) is seeking a Commissioning Project Manager to join its Mission Critical department. The selected candidate will represent the company in managing multimillion-dollar, time-sensitive projects for Mission Critical clients. This role involves leading teams of employees, subcontractors, and client vendors to execute critical systems infrastructure projects, including Data Centers, Financial Institutions, and Power Plants across North America.

Responsibilities:

Serve as a Commissioning Project Manager within a team of qualified professionals and degreed engineers.
Manage subcontractors and client vendors on a project-by-project basis.
Assign project tasks and schedules.
Act as a technical subject matter expert for complex mission-critical projects.
Develop procedures, methods, and testing scripts for power, hydraulic, and cooling systems for Data Centers, Financial Institutions, and Power Plants.
Lead client meetings, schedules, and issue resolution processes.
Prepare proposals for client RFPs and project pricing requests.
Assist with departmental budgets, KPIs, and financial planning for the Canadian region.
Review and ensure the accuracy of documentation from contractors, subcontractors, and vendors.
Oversee and validate the work of subcontractors on client projects.

Qualifications

Minimum 10 years of experience in the Electrical/Mechanical industry; a Bachelor's degree is preferred, but an Associate degree from relevant technical programs will be considered.
Equivalent combinations of education and experience are acceptable.
5-10 years of experience in commissioning complex installations and solving construction/operational problems.
Proven experience managing design, energy services, and commissioning projects within scope, budget, and schedule.
Familiarity with NETA, ASHRAE, LEED, and other building codes and industry standards.
Comprehensive understanding of Mission Critical systems related to MEP equipment in Data Centers and Power Plants.
Expertise in electrical systems, including high/medium voltage switchgear, main switchboards, backup generation, UPS systems, and power transfer equipment.
Proficiency in mechanical/thermal systems, such as HVAC equipment, chiller plants, evaporative cooling, and pumping systems.
Knowledge of plant control systems (BMS, SCADA, PLCs) and communication protocols (TCP/IP, Modbus, Canbus).
Familiarity with instrumentation for PID control loops.
Self-motivated with experience in MEP systems design, commissioning, retro-commissioning, and energy modeling for complex buildings.
Ability to perform construction observations, develop functional test plans, and execute tests for electrical and control systems.
Strong people and negotiation skills, time management, and problem-solving abilities.
Capable of explaining technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Fiscal awareness and ability to mentor direct reports.
P.Eng licensed in the U.S. or Canada (EIT or equivalent professional engineering membership accepted); preferred but not essential.
C.E.T. or equivalent with extensive commissioning experience.
LEED Associate and PMP certification preferred but not mandatory.
Canadian CSA Z462 Electrical Safety qualification or U.S. NFPA 70E equivalent.
Infrared Thermography certification preferred.
Proficiency in computer skills.

Work Environment:

Extensive local, national, and occasional international travel required (40-70% annually).
Typical travel days are Mondays and Fridays, with on-site work on Tuesdays, Wednesdays,
and Thursdays. Veolia provides employees the opportunity to return home on Fridays to
spend weekend with their families, unless specific work requirements necessitate
otherwise.

Occasional work outside normal business hours to accommodate maintenance windows
or weekend schedules.

Work environments include high-energy areas such as central plants, switchgear rooms,
and power transmission areas in Mission Critical facilities.

Additional Information:

The ideal candidate will work remotely from Toronto, Canada, with required travel. Veolia is an inclusive company committed to diversity and equal opportunity for all applicants.

Additional Information

Why join our team of researchers? Come and rejuvenate the world with us!

Acting today to create the world of tomorrow;
A company in constant growth;
A multitude of large-scale projects where you can put your talent to good use;
A multitude of large-scale projects where you can make the most of your talent; Challenges adapted to your needs and the absence of routine;
The possibility of developing your career according to your professional objectives;
Internal and external training and coaching programs;
A very competitive compensation, pension and benefits package;
Multi-disciplinary work teams and a health and safety oriented work environment.

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

Candidates must be immediately eligible to work legally in Canada; the employer will not sponsor candidates for a work permit or any other Canadian work authorization for this opportunity.

Veolia North America is committed to equal opportunity employment and advancement for all employees and potential employees, and to a work environment free from discrimination and harassment.

jobs.description:
Type de contrat

CDI

QUI SOMMES-NOUS

SUEZ permet à ses clients de fournir l'accès à des services d'eau et de déchets, par des solutions innovantes et résilientes. Présent dans 40 pays avec 40 000 collaborateurs, le Groupe permet également à ses clients de créer de la valeur sur l'ensemble du cycle de vie de leurs infrastructures et de leurs services, et de conduire leur transition écologique en y associant leurs usagers.

E&C (Engineering & Construction) est l’entité de SUEZ responsable de la conception et la construction des projets d’infrastructures d'eau et de traitement des déchets de toutes tailles et sur tous les continents. Ses équipes interviennent de l’appel d’offre jusqu’à l’exécution sur l’ensemble des projets EPC monde. Son savoir-faire technique, ses méthodes et ses procédés de traitement sont reconnus au niveau international.

VOTRE MISSION

Dans le cadre de notre développement, nous créons le poste de Purchasing Supply Chain Project Manager
pour les projets d'Infrastructures industriels EP/EPC en France et à l'étranger, dans les domaines du traitement de l'eau et des déchets, dans un contexte très dynamique.

En tant que Responsable Achats et Supply-Chain, vous serez directement rattaché au Directeur des Achats. Votre rôle consistera à assurer la coordination des achats et de la chaîne d'approvisionnement pour nos projets d'infrastructures de traitement en France et à l'International.

Vos Responsabilités

Définir la stratégie d'approvisionnement pour chaque projet dont vous aurez la charge, en collaboration avec la direction des achats, en vous appuyant sur les équipes d'acheteurs du groupe et les besoins spécifiques au projet.
Assurer la coordination d'une équipe composée d'acheteurs, d'expéditeurs et de logisticiens en fonction des besoins du projet, sous la direction du Project Manager.
Gérer les fournisseurs, assurer le suivi contractuel, négocier les avenants aux contrats et résoudre les litiges.
Négocier les prix et les conditions d'achat des équipements et des services nécessaires à la bonne exécution des projets.
Anticiper les besoins afin d'optimiser les résultats du projet.
Veiller au respect des délais, de la qualité et des coûts.
Élaborer les reportings nécessaires au suivi du projet et garantir la qualité des informations.
Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le Engineering Manager et le Project Manager pour élaborer des solutions compétitives adaptées aux enjeux du projet.

VOTRE PROFIL

Formation Ingénieur (généraliste, Mécanique) Avec Une Expérience Confirmée En Tant Qu'Acheteur Leader Ou Responsable Achats Dans Une Entreprise Industrielle. Vous Disposez Des Compétences Suivantes

Une expérience préalable dans le domaine du traitement de l'eau et des déchets serait un atout.
Curiosité, autonomie, méthode et rigueur sont des qualités essentielles.
Votre leadership et vos compétences en négociation vous permettront de réussir dans ce poste.
Force de proposition, vous êtes engagé(e) dans une démarche d'amélioration continue.
Niveau d'anglais courant requis, minimum.

Suez préserve l’équilibre entre vie professionnelle et privée, ce poste est ouvert au télétravail.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager – Environmental Planning & Permitting (CEQA)
jobs.description:
Woodard & Curran is an employee-owned engineering, science, and operations firm dedicated to clean water, a safe environment, healthy communities, and happy people. We foster an inclusive, collaborative culture that supports professional growth, flexibility, and meaningful work, empowering our employees to make a lasting impact on our clients, communities, and the planet.

What are we looking for:
Woodard & Curran is seeking a Senior Project Manager with 15+ years of environmental planning and permitting experience to support a growing portfolio of water resources, infrastructure, and environmental management projects throughout California and the West Coast. This individual will be a trusted advisor to clients, leading complex environmental review and permitting efforts while managing multidisciplinary teams, agency coordination, project delivery, and business development initiatives.

What’s in it for you?
Join a collaborative and employee-owned consulting firm where you'll have the opportunity to lead high-profile environmental planning and permitting projects, shape regulatory strategies for critical infrastructure investments, mentor emerging professionals, and contribute to strategic growth across the West Coast. You'll work alongside industry experts while helping clients navigate complex environmental challenges that make a positive impact on communities and natural resources.

Hybrid/Remote/Office Hybrid Or Remote (West Coast Preferred)

Location:
California or West Coast Region

Travel:
20% travel throughout California and the West Coast region for client meetings, project oversight, agency coordination, business development, and team collaboration.

What you will be doing at Woodard & Curran:

Serve as a trusted advisor to clients by identifying environmental regulatory risks and developing strategic solutions
Lead and manage complex CEQA (IS/MND, EIR) and NEPA (EA, EIS) environmental review and permitting projects from initiation through completion
Develop regulatory and permitting strategies that align with client objectives and project goals
Serve as the primary point of contact with regulatory agencies, stakeholders, and key project partners
Manage project scope, schedule, budget, forecasting, invoicing, and overall financial performance
Perform technical review and QA/QC of environmental documentation, technical studies, field data, and subconsultant deliverables
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams, including environmental specialists, engineers, and technical subconsultants
Support client relationship management and business development efforts for existing and prospective clients
Lead proposal development, strategic pursuits, and marketing initiatives
Mentor and develop junior staff, project managers, and technical professionals across distributed teams
Monitor project progress and technical delivery to ensure client satisfaction and successful outcomes

What will you need to succeed?

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Biology, Civil Engineering, Hydrology, Forestry, or a related discipline (Master's degree preferred)
Minimum 15 years of environmental planning and permitting experience supporting infrastructure, water resources, and site development projects
Minimum 8 years of project management experience in a consulting environment
Extensive knowledge of CEQA, NEPA, the Clean Water Act, and related California and federal environmental regulations
Proven experience leading agency coordination, environmental review processes, and permitting efforts
Established relationships with California and regional regulatory agencies, including RWQCB, SWRCB, CDFW, DWR, USACE, and USFWS
Experience developing permitting schedules, cost estimates, and environmental compliance programs
Familiarity with environmental inspection and monitoring requirements during construction
Strong understanding of infrastructure development and construction practices that minimize environmental impacts
Excellent technical writing, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills
Strong leadership, mentoring, and team management abilities
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Microsoft Dynamics 365
Existing network of environmental and technical subconsultants throughout California and the West Coast preferred

$170,000 - $230,000 a year

Final compensation will be determined based on these factors and adjusted, where applicable, by a geographic differential. Geographic differentials are percentage-based adjustments that reflect variations in labor market costs across locations. As a result, the compensation range for this position may vary depending on where the successful candidate is located and performs their work. As a Project Manager, you will lead and support Instrumentation and Controls (I&C) modernization projects for the operating fleet of nuclear power plants the Americas.

This critically important role will lead projects from offer development through design, build, test, and implementation. Being the owner of their projects, the PMs balance project constraints and leading teams to deliver project successfully for both internal and external stakeholders.

In this role, you will serve as a strategic leader driving complex, cross-functional due diligence initiatives, partnering closely with cybersecurity architects, engineers, legal counsel, and business leaders to translate technical security insights into clear, executive-ready risk recommendations.

Facilitate technical decision-making and risk governance across diverse stakeholder groups to enable informed acquisition and integration decisions

jobs.title: Microelectronics - Program Manager - Business Execution
jobs.description:
Aquatech’s Microelectronics business is entering a period of rapid global growth. Microelectronics Program Manager - Business Execution & Integration will support execution of the Microelectronics global strategy by establishing the structure, coordination, reporting, and accountability required to convert business priorities into completed actions and measurable results.

The role serves as an internal execution and organizational integrator, working across engineering, technology, project execution, commercial, supply chain, finance, HR, regional teams, and other Aquatech organizations. The Program Manager will coordinate cross-functional initiatives, develop and maintain implementation schedules, establish reporting and KPIs, manage organizational interfaces and stakeholder agreements, track commitments, and drive follow-through.

A significant emphasis of the position is working effectively within Aquatech’s matrix organization. The Program Manager will establish clear working agreements with internal and partner organizations regarding scope, responsibilities, resources, interfaces, deliverables, schedules, governance, and reporting. Success depends on creating organizational accountability and achieving results through coordination and influence rather than direct authority.

This is not a customer project-management or PMO position. Project managers and functional organizations retain accountability for customer projects and technical deliverables. This role applies program- and project-management discipline primarily to internal Microelectronics organizational, strategic, standardization, product-development, and business-improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Business Operating Rhythm & Accountability

Establish and maintain the Microelectronics operating cadence, dashboards, KPIs, action tracking, decision logs, business reviews, and reporting processes required to provide clear visibility into priorities, commitments, accountable owners, milestones, risks, resource requirements, and completion status.

Internal Program & Initiative Execution

Convert Microelectronics priorities into executable internal programs with defined scope, owners, schedules, milestones, dependencies, resources, KPIs, and completion criteria; coordinate implementation across functions and organizations while functional and technical teams retain ownership of their respective technical scope and deliverables.

Internal initiatives may include organizational integration, global execution-model implementation, engineering and execution standardization, product development and productization, process improvements, business systems, supplier strategies, and organizational or cultural change.

Global Strategy Execution & Organizational Infrastructure

Translate the Microelectronics global strategy into practical organizational actions by coordinating roles and responsibilities, decision rights, resource requirements, operating processes, governance, standardization, organizational interfaces, and implementation activities required to support global execution and continued growth.

Matrix Organization & Stakeholder Management

Develop and maintain effective working agreements across Microelectronics and partner Aquatech organizations, defining scope boundaries, responsibilities, shared resources, interfaces, deliverables, schedules, communication requirements, governance, reporting, and escalation paths while tracking commitments and reinforcing organizational accountability.

Initial Priorities

During The First Six Months, The Program Manager Should

Implement the Microelectronics Global Execution Model

Drive implementation and organizational adoption of the Microelectronics Global Execution Model by converting the defined strategy into a structured implementation program with clear organizational responsibilities, schedules, milestones, dependencies, governance, decision rights, KPIs, and completion criteria.

Maintain the integrated implementation schedule; coordinate activities across Microelectronics and partner Aquatech organizations; establish required stakeholder agreements; track commitments and dependencies; identify resource constraints and implementation barriers; facilitate resolution and escalation; and drive completion of actions required to embed the model into normal business operations.

Establish the Microelectronics Operating & Reporting Cadence

Implement a consistent business operating rhythm with defined reviews, reporting requirements, dashboards, KPIs, action tracking, decision tracking, and follow-through.

Establish practical mechanisms for measuring progress against business priorities and internal initiatives and for identifying overdue actions, resource constraints, dependencies, and issues requiring resolution.

Establish Organizational Interfaces, Governance & Accountability

Document and implement the working infrastructure required to operate effectively across the Microelectronics matrix organization and partner Aquatech organizations.

Define and maintain organizational interfaces, scope boundaries, stakeholder agreements, roles and responsibilities, decision rights, shared-resource expectations, communication requirements, governance, reporting, and escalation paths.

Develop practical dashboards and KPIs to provide visibility into implementation progress, organizational commitments, resource requirements, business performance, and critical risks. Track agreed actions and deliverables to completion and reinforce accountability across participating organizations.

Required Experience & Capabilities

Significant experience in program management, business operations, engineering, organizational transformation, or similar cross-functional execution roles.
Demonstrated ability to convert strategy and broad organizational objectives into structured implementation plans, schedules, milestones, owners, KPIs, and measurable results.
Strong program- and project-management discipline applied to internal organizational and business initiatives.
Experience developing dashboards, KPIs, reporting systems, governance processes, and management routines.
Strong business and financial understanding with the ability to organize and communicate business-performance information.
Demonstrated experience working in complex matrix organizations and coordinating work across functions, regions, and partner organizations.
Ability to establish clear stakeholder agreements regarding scope, responsibilities, interfaces, resources, schedules, deliverables, and accountability.
Strong organizational and analytical skills with disciplined action tracking and follow-through.
Ability to influence teams and reinforce accountability without direct reporting authority.
Clear, concise communication skills with the ability to organize complex issues into actionable information.
High degree of integrity, discretion, urgency, and sound judgment.

Preferred Experience

Experience in semiconductor, microelectronics, water treatment, industrial technology, engineering, construction, or capital-equipment businesses is preferred. Familiarity with ultrapure water, industrial wastewater treatment, water reuse, zero-liquid discharge, or semiconductor infrastructure is beneficial.

Experience implementing global operating models, coordinating geographically distributed organizations, developing internal standards and processes, or executing cross-functional organizational change is highly desirable.

Behaviors

Execution Focused – Converts strategy, plans, and decisions into structured actions and follows them through to completion.

Accountable – Establishes clear ownership, due dates, deliverables, and expectations and consistently tracks commitments.

Structured & Organized – Uses schedules, dashboards, KPIs, action registers, governance, and reporting to create visibility and maintain progress.

Collaborative & Influential – Works effectively across a matrix organization and obtains commitments from teams and partner organizations without relying on formal authority.

Fact Based – Uses data, KPIs, schedules, and documented commitments to identify issues and communicate status objectively.

Persistent – Maintains follow-through across functions and organizations and does not allow actions, decisions, or commitments to stall.

Practical – Focuses on implementation, removing organizational barriers, and creating processes that improve execution rather than adding unnecessary administrative complexity.

Adaptable – Adjusts priorities, schedules, and coordination as business conditions and organizational requirements change.

Reporting & Governance

Microelectronics Program Manager - Business Execution & Integration will report to the Vice Presidents of the Microelectronics Business Unit, with one VP designated as the primary day-to-day sponsor and performance-review owner.

The position is expected to operate primarily as an individual contributor working across a matrix organization. Functional, regional, engineering, project, and account organizations retain accountability for their respective scope and deliverables.

The Program Manager does not lead the Microelectronics PMO or assume responsibility for individual customer projects. The role provides the internal program-management structure, coordination, schedules, reporting, KPIs, stakeholder alignment, governance, and accountability mechanisms required to execute the Microelectronics global strategy and internal organizational initiatives.

Benefits

Aquatech offers a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, company-paid holidays, and a 401K plan (all benefits are based on eligibility).

Essential Functions

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed above and below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Physical Job Demands

Lifting/carrying/moving and exerting up to 50 lbs. of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects, including the human body. May need to climb ladders, cannot be afraid of heights, and will need to wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) while on site. It involves sitting at a desk for extended periods. Needs a high degree of concentration in a busy area.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Civil, or related discipline).

Job Description

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.

The Role

Advanced Vehicle Development is seeking an experienced Technical Project Manager to establish and operate a common work-management approach across program and project teams. This role will configure and administer Jira, develop work breakdown structure templates for different team types, facilitate effective Scrum execution, connect interdependent work across organizations, and create clear status views for executives, leaders, and delivery teams.

The successful candidate will help Advanced Vehicle Development improve execution visibility, cross-functional alignment, and delivery discipline while enabling teams to focus on the work required to advance vehicle architecture and technology development.

What You’ll Do (Responsibilities)

Establish and maintain Jira as a work-management solution for Advanced Vehicle Development program and project teams.
Define Jira workflows, issue types, fields, permissions, naming conventions, and operating guidelines that support consistent execution and reporting.
Create reusable work breakdown structure templates for different Advanced Vehicle Development team types, including program teams and technical project teams.
Translate program milestones and deliverables into appropriately structured epics, features, tasks, dependencies, and actionable work items.

Plan, facilitate, and continuously improve Scrum events, including planning, daily coordination, reviews, retrospectives, and backlog refinement.
Customize Scrum cadences, ceremonies, workflows, and reporting practices to fit the needs of specific team types while maintaining common program-level standards.
Partner with Scrum Managers, project managers, technical leads, and portfolio stakeholders across other organizations to connect related projects, dependencies, milestones, and deliverables.

Establish and maintain mechanisms for identifying, tracking, escalating, and resolving cross-organizational risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies.
Create and maintain multiple Jira dashboards and status views that provide the right level of information for each audience:
Executive View – overall health, major milestones, critical risks, decisions, and delivery confidence.
Leadership View – program progress, cross-team dependencies, capacity concerns, risks, and upcoming commitments.
Team View – backlog health, sprint progress, impediments, assigned work, and near-term priorities.

Define standard status metrics and reporting practices so that project information is timely, consistent, and decision-ready.

Coach teams on practical work-management, backlog-management, estimation, prioritization, and status-reporting practices.
Monitor adoption of the Advanced Vehicle Development work-management approach and identify opportunities to simplify processes and improve execution efficiency.
Develop concise leadership communications, operating reviews, training materials, and user guidance for Jira and related delivery practices.
Work with information technology and enterprise tool teams to address Jira integrations, access, data quality, automation, and reporting needs.

Protect confidential company information and follow applicable General Motors policies and procedures.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, information systems, project management, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
2+ years of experience in technical project management, program management, engineering operations, product development, or a related delivery environment.
Demonstrated experience organizing complex, cross-functional work into actionable plans, milestones, deliverables, and dependencies.
Experience facilitating project execution across multiple teams or organizations without direct authority.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to convert complex technical and organizational information into clear status, decisions, actions, and executive-level recommendations.
Strong analytical, planning, prioritization, problem-solving, and follow-through skills.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and adapt to changing program needs.

What Can Give You a Competitive Advantage (Preferred Qualifications)

Experience configuring, administering, or scaling Jira or a comparable work-management platform.
Experience with Scrum, Agile, Kanban, or other iterative delivery methods.
Experience creating work breakdown structures, delivery templates, project taxonomies, or portfolio-management standards.
Experience designing executive, leadership, and team dashboards using Jira or business-intelligence/reporting tools.
Experience connecting dependencies and integrated schedules across engineering, software, product, information technology, or other technical organizations.
Experience supporting vehicle development, advanced engineering, systems engineering, model-based systems engineering, or other complex product-development environments.
Jira, Scrum, Agile, or project-management certification.
Experience with workflow automation, dashboard design, data quality, or tool integration.
Demonstrated ability to build collaboration, influence adoption, and foster a culture of transparency and accountability.
Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, continuous-improvement mindset, and ability to champion change.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Imagine having the power to stress-test an entire power grid against a hurricane or thunderstorm before the clouds even gather. That is the reality we are creating at Neara.

We use advanced machine learning to create engineering-grade, physics enabled digital twins of electricity grids across four continents, this helps asset owners understand their biggest challenges and bring the most viable solutions to life across millions of kilometres of infrastructure.

By simulating extreme weather and structural stress at a network-wide scale, we empower the world’s largest utilities to pinpoint risks, optimise investments and build a more resilient global energy future.

Our team is a collection of brilliant minds who are fanatical about making a tangible difference in the real world, utilising AI and machine learning to accelerate everything from data classification to complex scenario analysis. We have built a special culture where innovation thrives because everyone owns the mission and we need smart, creative people to help us scale this impact to every corner of the globe.

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own delivery of complex, high-value programs for our largest US utility customers. This is a customer-facing role, where you will be the trusted point of contact for customer teams and executive sponsors. While our Customer Success team members will own technical excellence and delivering the value to customers, you will be accountable for delivering every program on time, to scope and to a standard of excellence that customers will remember.

You will be the connective tissue between Customer Success, Product and Engineering, and a champion for change with both customers - adopting new technology and ways of working - and inside Neara, as our delivery model evolves. That includes a relentless pursuit of ways to deliver more and larger customer projects with the same resources, using AI and automation to make our work faster, more consistent and more scalable.

What You’ll Do

Lead end-to-end delivery of a portfolio of complex enterprise programs, from kickoff through go-live and adoption, involving large-scale data ingestion (LiDAR, GIS, asset data), model builds, integrations and value driven use cases
Be the primary point of contact for customer program teams and executive sponsors, building trusted relationships at every level
Run program governance, incl. steering committees, executive updates, status reporting & decision logs
Define scope, milestones, dependencies and success criteria, and keep programs on track by coordinating across Customer Success, Product and Engineering
Plan ahead for risks and dependencies, and guide stakeholders through key decisions with clear options and trade-offs
Champion change with customers through stakeholder alignment, training and adoption plans, so new workflows become part of how teams work
Apply and improve program management standards, templates and reporting across the US team
Identify opportunities to use AI and automation across the delivery lifecycle, such as status reporting, data validation and project setup, and help the team adopt them

What You’ll Bring

5+ years in technical program or project management, delivering complex enterprise software, data or infrastructure programs
Significant customer-facing experience, comfortable leading the room with senior stakeholders and building lasting trust
A consistent record of delivering multi-stakeholder programs on time and to a high standard
A natural change leader who has helped customers and teams adopt new tools, processes or ways of working
Technical enough to go deep with engineers on data pipelines, integrations and cloud platforms. Python or SQL skills are highly regarded
Comfortable working at multiple altitudes: shaping program strategy with executives one day, unblocking execution on the ground the next
Confident with data, tooling and project management tools (e.g. Fibery, Jira, Asana), and a practical user of AI tools to improve how work gets done
Experience in utilities, energy, GIS or LiDAR is a plus but not essential

What We Offer

A rare opportunity to run some of our most important US customer programs while shaping how we deliver in one of our fastest-growing markets
Work on technology that matters. Our digital twins are actively protecting energy grids from increasingly common extreme weather and structural failure
Strategic autonomy, paired with a collaborative culture where everyone, from engineering to leadership, is accessible and aligned on the same mission
Competitive compensation including ESOP, flexible working, and excellent PTO, healthcare and 401(k) programs

Compensation Range: $150K - $200K

jobs.title: Sales Enablement Program Manager
jobs.description:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.
The Role
We’re looking for a proactive and highly organized Sales Enablement Program Manager to help drive clarity, consistency, and continuous learning across Block’s global sales and Account Management teams. You’ll play a critical role in operationalizing our everboarding strategy—ongoing education beyond onboarding. This role requires a strong blend of content operations, learning science, stakeholder management, and sales context awareness.
You Will
Support ongoing learning initiatives by helping to plan, build, facilitate, and maintain scalable sales enablement content beyond onboarding.
Curate and maintain centralized knowledge resources, partnering with subject matter experts (SMEs) across Product, Marketing, and Sales to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Help operationalize the everboarding strategy, coordinating timelines, deliverables, and stakeholder communications.
Organize and update internal learning assets, ensuring documentation is easy to find, up-to-date, and aligned with sales priorities.
Manage internal communications related to enablement, such as newsletters, training calendars, training decks, and update broadcasts to reduce noise and increase clarity.
Collect feedback and track program impact, using data to assess adoption, knowledge retention, and performance improvements.
Support regional Canada enablement needs, ensuring content is localized and relevant for diverse sales teams across markets.
Promote knowledge-sharing practices, including documenting playbooks, building FAQs, and contributing to internal wikis or LMS content.

You Have

4+ years of experience in Sales Enablement, Sales, or Account Management.
Strong understanding of adult learning theories and experience applying them to training design, content delivery, or knowledge-sharing systems.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with an ability to influence and collaborate across functions and levels.
Proven ability to prioritize effectively, manage competing demands, and maintain clarity under ambiguity.

Nice to Have
Background in instructional design, content strategy, or sales operations.
Exposure to coaching methodologies such as GROW to support learner development and behavior change.

We're working to build a more inclusive economy where our customers have equal access to opportunity, and we strive to live by these same values in building our workplace. Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.

ChicagoCAC employees are expected to perform their job duties and act in a manner consistent with the Core Values of the organization.

Responsibility Summary

The Program Manager of CAN Hope provides day-to-day supervision and operational leadership for the Chicago Advocacy Network for Hope (CAN Hope) family justice center program in its service to survivors of domestic and sexual violence, human trafficking, stalking, and other forms of interpersonal or community violence. This position supports the implementation of program priorities, operations, procedures, and leadership values as established by the Director. Survivor-centered and evidence-informed practices are integrated throughout all responsibilities.

DEI&AB Culture Commitment:
The Program Manager is responsible for creating an inclusive environment that demonstrates equity, inclusion, accessibility, and belonging to our clients, ChicagoCAC employees, and partners. The position also assists in ChicagoCAC’s Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, Accessibility and Belonging (DEIAB) initiatives.

Primary Responsibilities

Supervise direct services and staffing needs to ensure compliance with program expectations as established by the Director. Function in direct service roles as needed.
Maintain and support team access to relevant resources, evidence-informed practices, research, and specialized training relevant to survivor services.
Serve as a public steward of CAN Hope by building relationships with individuals, organizations, and institutions that support survivors and coordinate CAN Hope’s participation in outreach opportunities and community-based events.
Serve as site supervisor in the absence of or as assigned by the Director.
Support the Director in collecting, organizing, and utilizing program data.
Attend and participate in regularly scheduled meetings as relevant to the role.
Maintain program site cleanliness and organization as assigned.
Travel to ChicagoCAC’s other program sites and community locations as needed.
Regularly participate in ChicagoCAC sponsored client/staff/community events.

Discretion

The Program Manager exercises mid-level decision-making in managing routine program operations, supervising assigned staff, and resolving issues or conflicts within established ChicagoCAC policies, CAN Hope procedures, and the authority delegated by the Director. Significant changes to program procedures and operations require Director review and approval.

Supervisory Responsibilities

The Program Manager is responsible for direct supervision of CAN Hope’s direct service roles, interns, and volunteers as assigned.

Relationships

The Program Manager is expected to collaborate and work effectively with CAN Hope team members and partners, as well as ChicagoCAC peers and colleagues.

Qualifications

Minimum requirements:

Master’s degree in social work or a related field.
Three or more years of relevant social services experience.
Demonstrated experience supervising, leading, or coordinating the work of others with the ability to provide clear direction, establish consistent expectations, and use available tools and resources to support staff performance.
Demonstrated ability to give and receive feedback through curiosity, adaptability, sound judgment, and a solutions-oriented approach to problem-solving.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, as well as project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage deadlines, deliverables, direct service needs, and supervision requirements simultaneously.
Demonstrated cultural competency related to professional teamwork and support for survivors from various backgrounds.

Preferred Requirements

Five or more years of relevant social services experience.
Relevant professional licensure, certification, or specialized training, including LSW/LCSW, CDVP, Illinois 40-Hour DV Training and 40-Hour SV Training.
Bilingual in English and Spanish.

Benefits

In addition to making a significant impact on children’s and families’ lives, ChicagoCAC offers amazing benefits for our staff, which include:

BCBS HMO and PPO healthcare coverage options with an opportunity to add family members to plans.
Free life insurance at 2x your salary up to a maximum of $200,000. 
Additional pay of 5% of your salary up to $3,750 per year (available after 6 months of employment) to use towards a menu of benefits such as: additional health benefits, dental, vision, long-term disability short-term disability, 403b plan, a Roth option, legal coverage, dependent care, and flexible spending.
Paid Time Off (“PTO”): PTO starts accruing the first day of employment and accrues at a rate of 35 days in a 12-month period. 
PTO days are used for all days off, including holidays and sick time so you have maximum flexibility in the use of your PTO. 
Timing of vacations may be dependent on client needs, as that’s our first priority. 
PTO goes up to 40 days after 5 years. 
Additional PTO for FMLA-related reasons up to 20 days. 
A remote work policy that provides flexibility in work hours so long as operational needs are met. 
Regular expert training on evidence-based therapy modalities, which includes being able to earn Continuing Education Units. 
A casual dress code
Enjoy afternoon milk and cookies every Friday! 

If you share our passion for providing hope and healing to children and families who have experienced abuse and trauma, and possess the qualifications we’re looking for, please submit an application! 

ChicagoCAC’s Compensation Philosophy: 

We are committed to fair compensation, aligned with Chicago market rates. Our salary scale reflects our values, business strategy, and financial goals. Based on funding and internal equity, the starting salary for this position may fall between the minimum and midpoint of the listed range.

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: 

ChicagoCAC is an Equal Opportunity Employer: BIPOC, persons with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people are strongly encouraged to apply.

We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact our People & Culture Department at (312) 492-3700.

jobs.description:
Worker Type

Summary

Job Description

The Lead
Program Manager (PM)
is responsible for the execution of company programs including cost, schedule, and technical performance. The PM oversees program life-cycle and manages all activities necessary to meet business goals and objectives. Acting as the central focal point and authority for one or more Programs' execution, the PM provides a single point of contact for program activities to both internal and external customers

Position Responsibilities

Management of the program throughout the program's life-cycle. Ensures customer alignment and manage overall customer satisfaction
Definition, implementation, and management of program controls and success criteria. Identifies, analyzes, and manages all program-level risk
Coordinates and aligns project teams and their inter-dependencies. Establishes, communicates, and manages program priorities
Aligns and informs stakeholders of program's status and health. Leads program meetings and program reviews with the customer and executive staff
Develops and maintains program plans including budget, Estimate at Completion (EAC), resource allocation, and communications
Supports the creation and maintenance of product requirements
Manages potential changes in program scope and advise leadership and customer of potential impact
Actively supports the Business Development team in bidding and capturing opportunities
Assists and/or coordinates the preparation of cost and technical proposals
Ensures adherence to Company policies and processes
Other duties as assigned

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills & Experience)

Bachelor's degree in Business or Engineering related field is required or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience
Minimum 8 – 12 years of experience in Program Management
Proven track record of running multiple, successful projects
Experienced managing firm fixed price programs and developing risk management & mitigation plans
Experienced in a highly technical environment
Deep knowledge of Project Management methods, tools and processes
Proficient in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook and MS Project)
Some travel required (up to 20%)

Other Qualifications & Desired Competencies

PMI (or equivalent) certification is preferred
Experience with Unmanned Aircraft Systems is desired
Experience managing International (ex-US) programs is desired
Active Secret or Top Secret Security Clearance strongly desired
Other competencies: Strong verbal and written skills; analytical and strategic thinking ability; leadership skills; very strong work ethic as well as honesty, trustworthiness and high integrity
Interfaces effectively with internal teams as well as government and commercial customers
Works well independently and interface with cross-functional disciplines
Is a strong communicator who effectively articulates vision/mission to team
Demonstrates familiarity with use and application of export licenses for the export of military products to foreign countries
Courageous and a risk taker. A mover and shaker yet collaborative and inclusive of a team approach to results
Committed to AV Values (Trust & Teamwork, Customer Commitment, Ownership & Results, and Innovate & Simplify) and emulates these values in all actions
Able to excel in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, where small teams share a broad variety of duties
Displays strong initiative and drive to accomplish goals and meet company objectives
Takes ownership and responsibility for current and past work products
Is committed to learning from mistakes and driven to improve and enhance performance of oneself, others, and the company
Focuses on teamwork and puts the success of the team above one's own interests

Physical Demands

Required to sit and stand for long periods (Frequent); talk, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer and telephone keyboard (Frequent)
Ability to work in an office environment (Constant)

Special Requirements

U.S. Citizen required.

Clearance Level

No Clearance

The Salary Range For This Role Is

$116,500 - $177,500

AeroVironment considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the location, the role and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, education/training, and key skills.

In order to comply with the requirements of the ITAR and/or the EAR, applicants must qualify as a U.S. person under the ITAR and the EAR, or a person to be approved for an export license by the governing agency whose technology comes under its jurisdiction. : AV offers an excellent benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401K with company matching, a 9/80 work schedule and a paid holiday shutdown. For more information about our company benefit offerings please visit: http://www.avinc.com/myavbenefits.

We also encourage you to review our company website at http://www.avinc.com to learn more about us.

jobs.title: Pharmacist (Facility Program Manager - Pharmacy Benefits Manager)
jobs.description:
Summary

The VA Palo Alto Health Care System (VAPAHCS) has an immediate opening for a Pharmacist Program Manager - Pharmacy Benefits Manager to work at the Palo Alto Division. The Pharmacy Benefits Manager (PBM) position is a unique leadership position within Pharmacy Service that manages programs - not people and is unique to VA formulary and fiscal management.

Qualifications

Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Basic Requirements

United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy
English Language Proficiency: Pharmacists must be proficient in spoken and written English as required by 38 U.S.C. 7402(d) - and 7407(d)
Education: Graduate of an Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) accredited College or School of Pharmacy with a baccalaureate degree in pharmacy (BS Pharmacy) and/or a Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D. degree
(NOTE: Prior to 2005 ACPE accredited both baccalaureate and Doctor of Pharmacy terminal degree program
Today the sole degree is Doctor of Pharmacy)
TRANSCRIPTS MUST BE SUBMITTED WITH APPLICATION
Graduates of foreign pharmacy degree programs meet the educational requirement if the graduate is able to provide proof of achieving the Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Examination Commission (FPGEC) Certification - which includes passing the Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Equivalency Examination (FPGEE) and the Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT)
YOU MUST SUBMIT COPY OF FPGEC CERTIFICATION WITH THE APPLICATION PACKAGE
Licensure
Full - current and unrestricted license to practice pharmacy in a State - Territory - Commonwealth of the United States (i.e. - Puerto Rico) - or the District of Columbia
The pharmacist must maintain current registration if this is a requirement for maintaining full - current - and unrestricted licensure
A pharmacist who has - or has ever had - any license(s) revoked - suspended - denied - restricted - limited - or issued/placed in a probationary status may be appointed only in accordance with the provisions in VA Handbook 5005 - Part II - Chapter 3 - section B - paragraph 16
YOU MUST SUBMIT A COPY OF CURRENT LICENSE WITH THE APPLICATION PACKAGE
May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria)
Grade Determinations: GS-13 Facility Program Manager Experience: In addition to the GS-12 requirements - you must have 1 year of experience equivalent to the next lower grade level and must demonstrate the following knowledge - skills - and abilities (KSAs): 1
Ability to communicate orally and in writing to persuade and influence clinical and management decisions
2
Expert understanding of regulatory and quality standards for their program area
3
Ability to solve problems - coordinate and organize responsibilities to maximize outcomes in their program area or area of clinical expertise
4
Expert knowledge of a specialized area of clinical pharmacy practice or specialty area of pharmacy
5
Advanced skill in monitoring and assessing the outcome of drug therapies - including physical assessment and interpretation of laboratory and other diagnostic parameters Preferred Experience: Previous VA work experience in formulary management - Pharmacoeconomics - drug file management strongly preferred
Reference: For more information on this qualification standard - please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/
The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-13
The actual grade at which an applicant may be selected for this vacancy is GS-13
Physical Requirements: Must pass occupational health requirements
Work requires sitting - walking - standing - bending and lifting/carrying of light items
Extended Periods of working on a computer and being on the telephone.

Duties

The VA Palo Alto Health Care System (VAPAHCS) has an immediate opening for a Pharmacist Program Manager - Pharmacy Benefits Manager to work at the Palo Alto Division
The Pharmacy Benefits Manager (PBM) position is a unique leadership position within Pharmacy Service that manages programs - not people and is unique to VA formulary and fiscal management
This Health Care System is a teaching facility affiliated with Stanford University - School of Medicine - and University of the Pacific - School of Pharmacy
Responsibilities include (but are not limited to): Leadership duties: serves as a resource throughout the pharmacy service and other clinical services
facilitates and conducts process improvement activities within pharmacy service
all by utilizing effective interpersonal skills - systems thinking approach - flexibility and adaptability - organizational stewardship - technical - leadership and strong communication skills
Pharmacoeconomic Program Management duties: leads the group of three Pharmacoeconomic Pharmacists in the design - coordination - implementation and management of pharmacy-based programs aimed at optimizing the cost efficiency of selected medications/pharmacotherapy throughout the organization
This includes leading monthly Pharmacoeconomic team meetings
tracking all cost-savings initiatives through to completion and one-year post-implementation outcomes (clinical and financial)
tracking all prior authorization drug consults - decision support order sets (DSOS) - and medication use criteria for annual review and updates
conducting medication use evaluations including pulling data utilizing SQL
and precepting pharmacy residents (PGY1 and PGY2)
Pharmacy Benefits Management duties: tracks/trends/reports pharmacy budget expenditures monthly
projects and submits next annual pharmacy budget proposal
coordinates/tracks/trends attainment of National and VISN performance measures and metrics with the performance measure champions and provides guidance and mentoring to ensure meeting the metrics
leads the monthly Pharmacy Performance Measure Council (PPMC) meetings
serves as the Executive Secretary of the health care system Medication Management Committee (MMC - aka Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee) by preparing the agenda - minutes and summary - coordinating presentations - providing input/guidance to ensure thorough proposals and follow up to requestors
leads the Pharmacy Leadership pre-MMC meetings to ensure alignment and operations input before the meeting
collaborates with the Pharmacy Informatic Pharmacists and Clinical Applications Coordinators to ensure maintenance of the drug file - medication order sets - progress note templates - pulling data from SQL or fileman - and developing new dashboards where applicable
Work Schedule: Monday-Friday 8:00am-4:30pm Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position
Functional Statement #: 10539F Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Authorized Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized

The (USA) Staff, Technical Program Manager leads complex, medium- to high-complexity technology programs, aligning deliverables with strategic objectives while managing cross-functional dependencies. Join the GTP PMO Team at Walmart Global Tech’s Platforms organization, where we drive execution excellence across multiple technology domains. The team accelerates program delivery by managing risks, dependencies, and adoption efforts within Global Tech. Known for its focus on execution, automation, and strong relationship building, the team supports complex technology initiatives that impact millions daily. Prepares concise, logically structured reports/materials and communicates complex technical information clearly to large and varied audiences.

Demonstrated experience in planning, execution, and risk mitigation for medium to high-complexity initiatives.

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Req ID: 141426

Region: Americas

Country: USA

State/Province: Oregon

City: Portland

Summary

The Program Manager serves as the primary customer interface, driving program success for semiconductor customer accounts with a primary focus on New Product Introduction (NPI). The ideal candidate is a proven project leader with a track record of successfully delivering complex initiatives within dynamic matrix environments. They excel at navigating cross-functional dependencies, aligning multidisciplinary teams, and driving project velocity even when contributors are managing competing priorities across departments. Through persuasive leadership, clear prioritization, and proactive negotiation, they effectively resolve resource constraints to keep milestones on track without direct supervisory authority.

For smaller customer accounts the program manager acts as the primary interface to the customer for the purpose of managing specific programs and projects on behalf of the customer account to achieve the planned revenue and profits. This job is a first-level manager within a site. Provides direct management to semi-skilled and entry level professional employees performing diverse and/or specialized roles, or employees in more than one function or work group. This includes establishing annual plans/objectives and interpretation of policies related to the functional area. Contributes to policy development. Work is performed within established professional standards and practices. Receives assignments in the form of tasks and goals and follows established processes to meet the goals of the unit. Executes budgets, develops schedules, and enforces policies and procedures. Erroneous decisions or failure to achieve results may have a negative impact on the site's/departments operations, schedules, and/or performance goals. Provides immediate supervision to employees in more than one function or work group, assigning tasks and checking work at regular intervals. Directs subordinates to achieve assignments using established guidelines, procedures, and policies. Makes hiring and firing decisions. Reviews employees performance and recommends employee compensation; coaches for improved performance and disciplines as necessary. Interacts directly with subordinates and peer groups. Builds strong internal and external relationships that require exchanging of information and providing explanations in a problem solving capacity.

Detailed Description

Performs tasks such as, but not limited to, the following:

NPI & Account Management: Acts as the primary interface and relationship manager between key customer leadership and internal operational teams, specifically overseeing high-complexity NPI and managing large-scale, strategic account portfolios.

Description

Senior Project Manager

Drive Execution. Remove Roadblocks. Deliver Predictable Outcomes.

At Power Integrations, we develop innovative semiconductor technologies that power energy-efficient solutions used around the world. From consumer electronics and industrial applications to electric vehicles and renewable energy systems, our products help customers solve increasingly complex power conversion challenges.

We're looking for a seasoned Senior Project Manager who thrives at the intersection of technology, execution, and leadership. This is not a project coordinator role. It's an opportunity for an experienced execution leader to become a trusted partner to Business Unit and Engineering leadership, helping our teams bring innovative semiconductor products from concept to production with greater speed, transparency, and predictability.

If you're energized by driving complex projects, influencing across organizations, and helping teams make better decisions faster, we'd love to talk with you.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Project Manager, you will lead the execution of complex semiconductor product development projects across multiple functions and geographies.

You'll serve as the organization's independent view of execution, partnering closely with Business Unit leaders, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Applications, Packaging, and Test teams to ensure projects stay aligned, risks are surfaced early, decisions happen quickly, and commitments are met.

This Role Is Built Around a Clear Operating Model

Business Unit Leaders own product strategy, portfolio priorities, and business outcomes.
Functional Leaders own technical solutions and execution within their teams.
You own integrated project execution, cross-functional alignment, schedule predictability, dependency management, and delivery transparency.

Success in this role requires more than maintaining schedules. You'll anticipate issues before they become problems, identify resource constraints before they affect commitments, and help leadership teams make informed decisions that keep projects moving forward.

What You'll Do

Lead Complex Product Development Projects

Drive cross-functional semiconductor product development projects from concept through production release.
Build and maintain integrated project plans, schedules, milestones, and critical-path activities.
Ensure alignment across Engineering, Applications, Packaging, Test, Quality, Operations, Marketing, and Business Unit stakeholders.
Establish clear project objectives, deliverables, dependencies, and success metrics.
Drive accountability and execution across matrixed teams.

Manage the Critical Path

Own and actively manage integrated project schedules.
Identify bottlenecks, competing priorities, and resource constraints before they impact commitments.
Anticipate and address dependencies across multiple organizations and development phases.
Develop recovery plans when projects deviate from schedule expectations.
Maintain clear visibility into execution readiness and milestone achievement.

Enable Better Decisions

Facilitate discussions that drive timely, data-based decisions.
Clarify ownership and ensure actions are completed.
Escalate issues appropriately and proactively.
Help leadership understand tradeoffs, risks, and schedule impacts.
Create transparency and eliminate surprises.

Drive Cross-Functional Alignment

Serve as the central coordination point across technical and business functions.
Build strong partnerships while maintaining objective project oversight.
Resolve conflicts and remove barriers to progress.
Ensure organizational priorities are translated into executable plans.

Proactively Manage Risk

Identify execution risks early and assess potential impacts.
Drive mitigation planning and accountability.
Monitor project health, resource availability, and milestone readiness.
Surface issues before they become critical delays.
Provide leadership with a clear view of risks and opportunities.

Leverage Technology and AI

Utilize modern project management tools, analytics, and dashboards to improve visibility and predictability.
Apply AI-enabled solutions to automate status gathering, action tracking, reporting, and risk identification.
Use data and automation to reduce administrative work and focus on execution leadership.
Help advance scalable project management practices across the organization.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Operations, or a related field.
8+ years of project management experience in semiconductor, electronics, hardware, or other complex product development environment.
Demonstrated success leading large, cross-functional technical projects.
Strong understanding of semiconductor development lifecycles, including:

IC development and tapeout
Validation
Package development
Test development
Qualification
Manufacturing readiness
Production release
Experience managing critical paths, dependencies, resource constraints, and project risks.
Strong leadership and influencing skills within matrix organizations.
Exceptional communication and executive presentation capabilities.
Proven ability to drive accountability without direct authority.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a related field.
PMP, PgMP, Agile, or similar project management certification.
Experience leading global semiconductor development teams.
Familiarity with PLM, ERP, and portfolio management systems.
Experience implementing AI-enabled project management or workflow automation solutions.

What Success Looks Like

Within This Role, You Will

Become the organization's trusted source of execution transparency.
Deliver projects with greater predictability and fewer surprises.
Identify risks and resource challenges early enough to avoid missed commitments.
Accelerate decision-making through structured communication and thoughtful escalation.
Strengthen accountability across teams and functions.
Enable business and technical leaders to focus on strategy and innovation while you ensure execution stays on track.
Help Power Integrations continuously improve how complex product development projects are planned and delivered.

Why Power Integrations?

At Power Integrations, you'll work on technologies that make electronic devices and energy systems more efficient worldwide. You'll collaborate with talented engineers, business leaders, and operations teams while influencing projects that have a direct impact on our customers and our business.

This is a highly visible role with significant opportunity to shape execution excellence across the organization and help deliver the next generation of industry-leading semiconductor product.

If you're passionate about driving clarity, alignment, accountability, and execution in a complex technical environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Power Integrations is committed to building teams that drive innovation and therefore review a range of factors when determining compensation. The annual base pay range for this position is $187,000 and $260,000. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, qualifications and work location.

The range displayed on the job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for this position in California. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Power Integrations also offers to our eligible employees a comprehensive total rewards package that includes equity, medical benefits, ESPP, 401K, tuition reimbursement and time off programs.
