jobs.title: Deputy Program Manager for Security & Protection - Active Clearance Required
jobs.description:
Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We have an opening for a Deputy Program Manager
(DPM) for the Security and Protection (S&P) Program within the Security Organization (SO). The S&P DPM is responsible for general oversight and personnel management of all S&P sections; in research and development (R&D), manufacturing, quality and assurance (QA), order compliance, systems and equipment distribution, as well as viability and operations in support of high-end security systems and associated technologies. In this position you will manage a multi-disciplinary team of scientists, software programmers, engineering/ technical staff, quality assurance, and administrative personnel, while being responsible for all areas of program management, high-level goal setting, and the development of strategies.

You will be responsible for assisting with the execution of the program’s annual operating plan (AOP) to meet objectives and deliverables by the NNSA Office of Defense Nuclear Security (NA-70), as well as Strategic Partnership Programs. This position is in the National Security Engineering Division (NSED) within the Engineering Directorate.

Depending on your assignment, this position may offer a hybrid work arrangement, blending in-person and virtual presence. You may have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.

This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level.

You will

Provide leadership and technical oversight to the multi-disciplinary team including matrixed full-time employees (FTE’s) from directorates throughout the laboratory, as well as contractors.
Manage cross-sectional (Software Development, IT Management, Systems Engineering, and Enterprise Communications) projects and logistical workflow.
Provide leadership and managerial oversight S&P’s Annual Operating Plan (AOP), including the allocation, monitoring of available personnel, and a ~$30M-$40M dollar budget.
Provide oversight and guidance of S&P’s annual operating budget and effort.
Lead recruiting, hiring, mentoring and the development of high-quality staff to support program sections and assist in their professional growth and advancement in technical and security areas.
Participate in NA-70/713 enterprise collaborative meetings and ensure S&P’s scope of work is clearly defined and advocate for and support development of appropriately funded scope. Effectively interface with other national laboratories and industry partners as part of the collaboration team.
Establish relationships with Department of Energy (DOE) enterprise sites security managers, system owners, personnel, and federal office personnel, including the Livermore Local Field Office (LFO).
Develop Work for Others (WFO's) proposals for the development of new security technologies.
Travel to DOE enterprise and industry partner sites in support of S&P projects, NA-70/713 discussions, DOE enterprise site visits, and industry partner meetings.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Additional Job Responsibilities, At The SEL.5 Level

Develop strategic initiatives to ensure the ongoing success of the whole enterprise consisting of seven (7) sites throughout the country, while creating a roadmap of future enterprise initiatives in collaboration with all stakeholders. Brief work to senior management on overall impact and approach.
Cultivate relationships with NNSA sponsors and technology leaders, while providing technical input and developing or refining new concepts in support of nuclear security priorities that promote LLNL skills, expertise, and technologies.
Cultivate and build relationships with other potential customers across the DOE, and Work for Others (WFO) (i.e., Department of Defense (DoD), and others) looking for additional program sponsors for new business opportunities.

Qualifications

This position requires an active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Nuclear Security or related discipline, or the equivalent combination of education and extensive related experience.
Significant experience solving complex system engineering problems in physical security systems or industrial control systems, intrusion detection systems, with in-depth experience in specialized areas.
Ability to motivate and collaborate effectively with other personnel in achieving project objectives.
Expert level experience leading complex programs and a proven record of resolving program management issues, as well as negotiating statements of work, timelines, and deliverables.
Expert level experience leading, tracking, and budgeting projects that require the application of creative innovation in managing and resource conflict resolution.
Ability to delegate effectively to accomplish goals within a multi-disciplinary team through leadership and positive influence, providing corrective measures when necessary.
Experience working with sponsors/government agencies, such as, NNSA, DOE, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), DOD, or other government agencies.
Expert communication, facilitation, and collaboration skills necessary to effectively present, explain, influence, and advise at all levels from staff to senior management.

Additional Qualifications At The SEL.5 Level

Expert knowledge of state-of-the-art technologies in physical security systems or industrial control systems.
Extensive experience successfully managing and leading multidisciplinary project teams with a successful history of producing high-quality cutting-edge technical products.
Extensive experience working with sponsors/government agencies, such as, NNSA, DOE, DHS DoD, or other government agencies.
Extensive experience developing and articulating strategic initiatives, and the ability to integrate and implement new programs and/or operational best practices.
Ability to champion, lead, and develop innovative cutting-edge technologies, theories, and concepts.

Pay Range

$227,430 - $346,140 Annually

$227,430 - $288,396 Annually for the SEL.4 level

$272,970 - $346,140 Annually for the SEL.5 level

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Additional Information

Position Information

This is a Career Indefinite position, open to Lab employees and external candidates.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
Flexible Benefits Package
401(k)
Relocation Assistance
Education Reimbursement Program
Flexible schedules (*depending on project needs)
Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

Security Clearance

This position requires an active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at time of hire.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How To Identify Fake Job Advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. jobs.description:
Taken en verantwoordelijkheden

Hoe maak jij mee het verschil?

Als Project Manager bij de afdeling Passenger Transport & Security, ben je verantwoordelijk voor de oplevering van kwaliteitsvolle oplossingen die inspelen op de behoeften van de interne klant. De projecten kunnen onder meer betrekking hebben op reizigersinformatie (real-time informatie), het aanbieden van alternatieve diensten, enzovoort.

Je hebt een directe impact op de tevredenheid van onze collega's en reizigers.

Wat is jouw rol bij NMBS?

Als Project Manager Voer Je Onderstaande Taken Uit

Je coördineert en volgt verschillende projecten op:

Je identificeert en formuleert de noden en verwachtingen van de business en de reizigers.
Je definieert concrete deliverables en tussenstappen, stelt vervolgens een projectplanning op, bepaalt de nodige middelen en beheert het budget. Daarnaast volg je nauwgezet de vooruitgang van het volledige project op.
Je waakt over de correcte toepassing van de regels en procedures en beheert de risico’s. Indien nodig neem je corrigerende maatregelen.
Je stemt af met de opdrachtgever gedurende het project.
Je communiceert naar interne en externe stakeholders (IT, operationele diensten, andere vervoersmaatschappijen, Infrabel, …).
Je ziet erop toe dat het project binnen de vooropgestelde termijn wordt afgerond.
Je staat in voor het opmaken en beheren van de projectdocumentatie.

Je werkt actief mee aan het opstellen van een projectroadmap.
Je waakt over de kwaliteit van de informatie.
Je stuurt functioneel een team aan.

Waarom is deze job iets voor jou?

Je beschikt over een masterdiploma (of gelijkwaardig door ervaring) EN een eerste ervaring van minstens 5 jaar in Project Management.

EN Je Beschikt Over De Volgende Vaardigheden

Je hebt goede communicatieve vaardigheden en bent in staat om zowel in het Frans als in het Nederlands te communiceren en te onderhandelen met je interne klanten.
Je hebt ervaring in zowel Agile als Waterfall project management.
Je beheert rapporterings- en presenteertechnieken.
Je passie voor IT zorgt ervoor dat je een complexe wirwar aan informatie kan ontcijferen en omzetten in hapklare en begrijpbare taal.
Door je teamgeest kun je een voorbeeld zijn voor je collega's, vooral op het gebied van samenwerking en communicatie.
Je bent leergierig en volgt de laatste evoluties (o.a. social media, agile, cloud).
Je bent assertief en resultaatgericht.
Beschik je over een PMP en/of SAFe-certificiëring, heb je kennis van kwaliteitszorgsystemen of van PM²? Die zijn pluspunten.

Indien je jouw diploma in het buitenland hebt behaald, dien je in het bezit te zijn van een gelijkwaardigheidsattest afgeleverd door de Vlaamse Overheid (NARIC-Vlaanderen) om deel te kunnen nemen aan de selectie.

We vinden het dan ook belangrijk dat je jezelf kan zijn. Want dat maakt NMBS sterker. Daarom hechten we veel belang aan diversiteit en inclusie.

Wat mag je van ons verwachten?

Kiezen Voor NMBS Is Kiezen Voor Een Omgeving Waarin Je Kan Bijleren En Groeien. Je Wordt Gesteund En Omringd Door Fijne Collega's. We Bieden Je Een Loonpakket Dat Bestaat Uit

Een aantrekkelijk salaris aangevuld met een 13e maand, onkostenvergoeding, maaltijdcheques en een collectieve en individuele bonus.
Een deel van het salaris wordt aangeboden als een flexibel budget. Je kan daarbij kiezen voor fietslease, lease auto, terugbetaling pensioensparen, ...
Een hospitalisatie- en groepsverzekering.
Flexibele werkuren, de mogelijkheid om te telewerken en 33 vakantiedagen per jaar.
Een treinabonnement in België, kortingen op internationale treinreizen en een fietsvergoeding.
Voordelen voor je gezin: o.a. kortingen op gezinsactiviteiten en in winkelketens.

Waar ga je werken?

Je werkt in de buurt van het station Brussel-Zuid.

What’s next?

Je solliciteert online.
We screenen je CV en motivatiebrief. We bellen je eventueel op om kennis te maken en om je kennis van het Frans te bevragen.
We nodigen je uit voor een eerst (online) sollicitatiegesprek waarin je je motivatie en competenties kan tonen. Ter voorbereiding op dit gesprek vragen we jou om een online persoonlijkheidsvragenlijst in te vullen.
Verloopt alles positief? Dan doen we je een contractvoorstel.
Je start in je nieuwe job!

Wij behouden ons het recht om deze procedure aan te passen of op te schorten indien nodig. Ons rekruteringsteam zal de profielen selecteren die het best aansluiten bij de functie-eisen om een optimale match te garanderen.

Husky TechnologiesTM a company with a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships, a strong sense of community and a unique culture and values. We are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM Canadian manufacturing facilities and global headquarters are located in Bolton, Ontario on a large, beautiful campus located just 20 minutes north of Toronto’s Pearson International Airport. Features include a fitness and wellness center, intramural sports activities, on-site cafeteria, and clean, state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities with outstanding safety records. We offer a great work environment and competitive total compensation package, including above market retirement savings plan and market competitive group benefits.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

Salary Range: 110k-142k

Replacement

The Global Trade Compliance team operates across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions in close collaboration with Husky’s Legal department. The team defines, implements, and continuously improves processes and policies to ensure compliance with global export control, sanctions, and customs regulations.

As the Global Trade Compliance Program Manager, you will report to the Director, Global Trade Compliance & Customs and serve as the program lead for enterprise-wide trade compliance initiatives. This role will focus on managing global compliance projects, optimizing processes, and ensuring the successful integration of trade compliance requirements into Husky’s systems.

You will partner with cross-functional teams—including Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, Finance, and Sales—to strengthen Husky’s global trade compliance framework, enhance operational efficiency, and reduce compliance risk across all regions.

Key Responsibilities

Program and Project Management

Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of global trade compliance initiatives, including process optimization, technology integration, and system enhancements.
Manage the implementation of trade compliance modules within the ERP system to ensure alignment with global regulatory requirements.
Establish and maintain project governance, milestones, KPIs, and reporting mechanisms for trade compliance programs.
Coordinate global stakeholders to ensure timely completion of key deliverables and consistent global deployment of compliance practices.

Regulatory Compliance and Oversight

Stay current on international trade laws, import regulations/tariffs, export control regulations, and sanctions programs applicable to Husky’s business activities.
Translate complex regulatory requirements into actionable business processes and internal controls.
Collaborate with Engineering and Legal teams to establish export control measures and export authorization processes globally.
Monitor the effectiveness of trade compliance procedures and implement corrective actions as needed.

Classification, Licensing, and Documentation

Lead efforts to standardize global product classification processes, including export control, HTS, and country-of-origin determinations.
Develop and maintain processes for end-use/end-user certifications, license applications, and transaction due diligence.
Ensure accuracy and consistency in trade data, documentation, and system configurations supporting export and customs compliance.

Risk Management and Continuous Improvement

Conduct global risk assessments and audits to evaluate compliance performance and identify improvement opportunities.
Develop risk mitigation strategies to prevent export control or import customs violations.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging digital tools and automation to enhance compliance monitoring and reporting.
Support internal investigations and voluntary disclosures, when applicable.

Training, Communication, and Stakeholder Engagement

Develop and deliver global training programs to increase awareness of export control, sanctions, and customs requirements.
Promote a culture of compliance through proactive communication and cross-functional collaboration.
Partner with IT, Supply Chain, and Finance to ensure trade compliance considerations are embedded in business processes.
Provide input in communications with government authorities and external consultants regarding trade compliance projects and inquiries.

Required Experience & Education

10+ years of progressive experience in global trade compliance, covering export controls, customs, sanctions, and trade agreements.
Deep understanding of U.S., EU, and Canadian export control and sanctions laws, with additional experience in UK, Swiss, Chinese, and other jurisdictions considered an asset.
Proven track record in managing large-scale trade compliance or ERP integration projects within a multinational organization.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, International Business, Law, Supply Chain, or related discipline; PMP or other project management certification preferred.
Strong analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to interpret complex regulations and translate them into practical business solutions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of influencing and engaging stakeholders across multiple levels and functions.
Demonstrated ability to lead change, manage competing priorities, and deliver results under tight deadlines in a global environment.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. You will be expected to identify opportunities where AI can augment human decision-making, reduce manual effort, and improve the speed and quality of execution across the revenue organization.

You will operate with growing autonomy and produce work that leaders across the revenue organization rely on, while continuously looking for smarter, more scalable ways to solve problems and improve how RevOps operates.

Our Guiding Principles

Be Bold. We pursue the biggest problems in our industry, challenge assumptions others take for granted, and take calculated risks to get there. We don't hide behind consensus or committees. Playing it safe is just failing slowly.
Help Customers Win. We learn our customers' businesses deeply — how they think, how they deploy capital, what keeps them up at night. We treat their capital like our own. We ship leverage, not features. And we measure ourselves by customer results, not our intentions.
Move with Urgency & Purpose. We bias toward delivery over perfection, remove friction from our own paths, and communicate in real time. Momentum compounds — and we build it every day.
Own the Outcome. We own outcomes, not just tasks. We hold a high Say:Do ratio and take responsibility from idea through impact. When something breaks, we fix it — we don't wait to be asked.
Never Satisfied. We raise the bar continuously. We stay curious, hold exacting standards, debate hard, and hold our opinions loosely when the evidence shifts. Excellence is a habit, not an event.

What You'll Do

Keep the revenue engine running. Run the weekly pipeline review process in Salesforce. Identify stale opportunities, missing next steps, and changes to close dates or deal values that could affect the forecast; work with account owners to resolve them.Connect the customer lifecycle. Work across Marketing, Sales, Deal Desk, Finance, and Customer Success to coordinate handoffs from lead through closed-won, invoicing, expansion, and renewal. Make sure each team has the information and ownership needed to move forward. Help deals move cleanly from sale to revenue. Review closed-won deals for documented approvals, signed terms, products, lines of business, pricing types, and revenue assumptions. Resolve gaps before they create problems for forecasting, billing, or customer handoffs. Make the numbers trustworthy. Compare opportunities, deal documentation, billing inputs, and financial reports to identify missing or inconsistent revenue streams. Support invoice questions by checking billed amounts against contracts and amendments, and track discrepancies through resolution with Finance and account teams. Challenge what the reporting says. Review existing dashboards and recurring reports for sound definitions, accurate inputs, and results that reflect what is happening in the business. Use AI and other tools to test assumptions, investigate anomalies, and recommend changes to reporting logic. Improve forecast reliability. Maintain forecast inputs and compare projected bookings and revenue with actual results. Investigate differences, question the assumptions behind them, and work with stakeholders to improve future forecasts. Find and fix operational friction. Document recurring processes, clarify handoff ownership, and address the delays or errors that repeatedly slow down deals, billing, and reporting. Support smarter planning. Provide historical analysis and scenario support for territory, quota, and revenue planning. Make good processes easier to repeat. Use automation and approved AI tools to reduce manual work, catch exceptions earlier, and make recurring validation more efficient.

What You'll Bring

2–4+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Deal Desk, Finance Operations, or a related analytical and operational role — ideally within SaaS, fintech, or another complex B2B revenue environment where you have worked across the customer lifecycle from pipeline through closed-won, billing, expansion, and renewal.

An AI-native approach to operations. You are curious about how AI and automation can fundamentally improve how work gets done. You look beyond using AI to complete individual tasks faster and identify opportunities to redesign workflows, automate repetitive validation, surface exceptions earlier, and improve the speed and quality of decision-making.
A process-improvement mindset. You notice recurring friction, unclear ownership, manual work, and points where information breaks down across the revenue lifecycle. You can document the current process, identify the root cause, and recommend a more scalable way of operating.
Demonstrated ownership and cross-functional follow-through. You can independently manage recurring operational processes and analytical work, coordinate across Sales, Marketing, Deal Desk, Finance, and Customer Success, and proactively resolve gaps rather than simply identifying them.
Strong analytical judgment and attention to detail. You don't take a report or data point at face value. You question definitions and assumptions, investigate anomalies, validate information against source data, and distinguish between a reporting issue and something happening in the underlying business.
The ability to turn analysis into action. You can explain what the data is telling us, why it matters, and what should happen next. You communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders and follow issues through resolution.

What Success Looks Like At Six Months

You understand how the revenue lifecycle connects end to end. You can trace a customer from lead through closed-won, invoicing, expansion, and renewal; understand the critical data and ownership required at each stage; and recognize when a breakdown upstream will create problems downstream.
Revenue data is more trustworthy because of your work. You can reconcile information across Salesforce, deal documentation, billing inputs, and financial reporting, identify the source of discrepancies, and drive issues through resolution with Finance and account teams.
You are actively contributing to RevOps becoming an AI-native function. You have identified and implemented at least one meaningful use of AI or automation that goes beyond individual productivity — redesigning a recurring workflow, automating validation, surfacing exceptions earlier, or improving the speed and quality of operational decision-making.
You are operating with meaningful independence. You manage recurring RevOps responsibilities and analytical work with limited oversight, prioritize effectively, meet deadlines, and proactively surface risks, inconsistencies, and opportunities rather than waiting for someone to ask.
Cross-functional partners trust you to help solve problems, not just report them. Sales, Marketing, Deal Desk, Finance, and Customer Success increasingly rely on you to investigate issues, connect information across teams, clarify ownership, and help drive problems through resolution.

AI & Technology Expectations

Bring experience using Salesforce and Gong to manage pipeline, surface customer insights, and inform sales strategy.
Leverage AI tools to enhance the productivity, quality, and speed of your work.
Use AI to support drafting, analysis, summarization, and problem-solving across your role.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort through automation and AI.
Apply AI to sharpen decision-making and strengthen strategic insights.
Share effective AI use cases and best practices with your team.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Analyst I or II (we are open to hiring at either level) to join the Statistics and Data Science department and support a diverse range of research projects. At NORC, Data Analysts are early career team members who train and work with our Statisticians and Data Scientists to perform tasks such as data processing, quality assurance, analysis, and dissemination.

As part of their data processing responsibilities, Data Analysts import, clean, standardize, transform, and validate data sets. They also research and document data procedures and support the investigation of data problems. They may identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns in data sets, support modeling efforts, and help prepare data presentations and reports, including developing charts, graphs, and tables. In addition, the Data Analyst may assist in data collection and harmonization from primary or secondary data sources (e.g., administrative records, commercial data, social media data), preparing data files for delivery, and the maintenance of databases, data systems, and their relevant metadata/dictionaries. The Data Analyst is expected to work collaboratively in a team environment.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location
: This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office.

DEPARTMENT: Statistics and Data Science

The Statistics and Data Science (SDS) department provides the scientific foundation required to advance NORC’s project portfolio. SDS delivers rigorous, innovative, and fit-for-purpose solutions along the project lifecycle. The department provides leadership for NORC’s approach on a broad range of approaches for study design and the analysis of primary and secondary data. SDS expertise includes artificial intelligence and machine learning; Bayesian analysis; causal inference; disclosure avoidance; imputation; data linkage and statistical matching for combining multiple data sources; data quality assessment; efficient and reproducible workflow development; privacy-preserving methods; small area estimation; statistical methods for survey sampling, weighting, estimation, and inference; and visualization.

The SDS department works closely with research, technology, and operational teams across NORC to ensure that statistical excellence and innovation remain central to the organization’s work. Many of NORC’s projects and proposals are led by substantive research departments that require significant contributions from SDS staff. SDS works closely with highly collaborative groups across the organization to ensure success through cross-departmental partnerships. To further capture the innovative spirit of NORC, SDS also leads projects that target departmental focus areas. Examples of recent project topics involving SDS staff include survey design, weighting, and analysis; AI for enhancing data quality, standardization, and integration; enhancing traffic safety data; linkage of health administrative data and surveys; and testing data visualization approaches for effective communication.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with statisticians, data scientists, technology experts, and subject matter experts to implement and improve data management and analysis activities.
Develop programs and scripts for data cleaning, integration, transformation, and harmonization, as well as data quality checks and validation
Support and enhance applications and databases already built for various research needs and produce data documentation and dictionaries.
Create data dashboards and visualizations, including preparing charts, graphs, and tables for reports and presentations.
Perform various types of data analysis and modeling, often involving multiple data sets.
Contribute to documentation, reports, and presentations through writing sections, creating basic analytic summaries, and developing tables and graphics.
Apply AI tools to help improve efficiency.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in statistics, data science, computer science, or an equivalent field.
0-2 years’ relevant experience (internships included).
Statistical programming in multiple packages and databases, including Python (required)
Familiarity working with large data sets, conducting statistical and quantitative modeling with strong programming.
Strong foundation in areas of analytic methods, data engineering, machine learning, and scientific methods of inquiry.
Experience with data management, data reduction techniques and data visualization.
Working knowledge of different types of data that can be sourced whether from administrative data, surveys, social media, or sensor data.
Strong skills in problem solving and quantitative analysis are required, including a willingness to understand deviations and ask questions about data issues.
Able to organize and prioritize work assignments to meet project needs.
Strong communication, writing and data storytelling skills.
Enthusiasm for teamwork and collaboration across disciplinary boundaries.

Preferred Skills

Preferred Skills:

Experience working with SAS, Tableau, Hadoop, Hive, Databricks, MapReduce, and/or other large data systems
Additional expertise in large and small language models, and machine learning, in working in cloud environments (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), and with command-line workflows (e.g., in bash)
Experience with JavaScript programming.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. now and in the future. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.

Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $62,000-$73,000.

Benefits

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment
Dental and vision insurance
A defined contribution retirement program, along with a separate voluntary 403(b) retirement program
Group life insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance
Benefits that promote work/life balance, including generous paid time off, holidays; paid parental leave, bereavement leave, tuition assistance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

NORC is committed to equity and transparency in its pay practices. We publish salary ranges and benefit information for every job. The listed hiring range reflects what we, in good faith, expect to pay at the time of posting, though actual compensation may vary and may be adjusted over time. A candidate’s placement within the range depends on factors such as competencies, education, qualifications, experience, skills, performance, and organizational needs.

What We Do

NORC at the University of Chicago is an objective, non-partisan research institution that delivers reliable data and rigorous analysis to guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions. Since 1941, our teams have conducted groundbreaking studies, created and applied innovative methods and tools, and advanced principles of scientific integrity and collaboration. Today, government, corporate, and nonprofit clients around the world partner with us to transform increasingly complex information into useful knowledge.

Who We Are

For over 80 years, NORC has evolved in many ways, moving the needle with research methods, technical applications and groundbreaking research findings. But our tradition of excellence, passion for innovation, and commitment to collegiality have remained constant components of who we are as a brand, and who each of us is as a member of the NORC team. With world-class benefits, a business casual environment, and an emphasis on continuous learning, NORC is a place where people join for the stellar research and analysis work for which we’re known, and stay for the relationships they form with their colleagues who take pride in the impact their work is making on a global scale.

Eeo Statement

NORC is an equal opportunity employer. NORC evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, sexual orientation, and other legally protected characteristics.

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY:

The Research Data Analyst 3 will independently support data management and analysis for one or more domestic and international research projects. Responsibilities will include designing data collection instruments and REDCap databases; developing data dictionaries and standard operating procedures; overseeing data collection, validation, cleaning, integration, and documentation; training and supporting project staff; monitoring data quality and timeliness; and resolving data discrepancies with collaborating research sites. In collaboration with investigators and biostatisticians, the analyst will conduct statistical analyses using established methods, interpret findings, prepare tables, figures, and reports, and contribute to abstracts, manuscripts, and scientific presentations. The analyst will manage competing priorities across projects and communicate effectively with multidisciplinary collaborators while ensuring compliance with applicable research protocols and data privacy and security requirements.

The RDA 3 will support several projects, however the primary project will be Rapid Research in Diagnostics Development for TB Network (R2D2 TB Network):
This NIH-funded project has established a platform to identify promising early-stage TB diagnostics and conduct field evaluations to assess their accuracy, usability, acceptability, and cost-effectiveness. The project includes research sites in Uganda, Zambia, Vietnam, India, and the Philippines. The analyst will support multicountry data systems, collaborate with international research teams, monitor data quality, and prepare analysis-ready datasets. Depending on experience and project needs, the position may also contribute to human factors research, Bayesian analyses, and health economic studies.

Department Summary

The UCSF Center for Tuberculosis (CTB) unites a multidisciplinary community of TB experts working to accelerate global TB elimination and train the next generation of TB scientists. Since launching in 2019, CTB has grown to include more than 50 faculty investigators across UCSF and UC Berkeley, spanning immunology, data science, epidemiology, pharmacology, diagnostics, therapeutics, biostatistics, implementation science, and policy. As the operational hub of the NIH P30-funded UC Tuberculosis Research Advancement Center, CTB serves as the scientific home for the TB research enterprise at UCSF and beyond. Through cooperative scholarship, technical training, mentorship, clinical excellence, advocacy, and a collaborative spirit, CTB-affiliated faculty, fellows, and staff are advancing global health and improving the lives of TB-affected communities through transformative research and practice.

The Institute for Global Health Sciences (IGHS) is a UCSF campus wide interdisciplinary program that reports to the Chancellor. IGHS is structured as an Organized Research Unit (ORU) and control point that oversees a portfolio of $330M in sponsored programs (including $80-90M per year in grants and cooperative agreements expenses), two graduate groups that confer Masters and PhD degrees, and an administrative unit that provides communication, financial management, event planning, staffing support, operations, and program development support to faculty members working in global health across the campus.

IGHS's mission is to advance health and reduce health disparities worldwide, with a focus on vulnerable populations. IGHS is continuing to expand its programmatic activities into new regions (Latin America and Asia) and new themes (e.g., transdisciplinary research in infectious disease, maternal and child health, and non-communicable diseases, pandemic preparedness, digital health, climate change, and migrant health). It also is working to develop new educational program offerings (degree and certificate) and partnerships with academic institutions in the US and in low- and middle-income (LMIC) countries. It also has engagements domestically with public health programs, including the California Department of Public Health.

IGHS is committed to ensuring a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment as we work towards becoming an anti-racist organization. We strongly encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds. Please see our statement on anti-racism here: https://globalhealthsciences.ucsf.edu/about-us/diversity-equity-and-inclusion/statement-structural-racism

Required:

Bachelor's degree in epidemiology, public health, or related area and 3 years of directly relevant work experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Thorough knowledge of research function.

jobs.description:
NRG is a leading global insights and strategy firm at the confluence of content, culture, and technology. We stay ahead of what ’ s next, providing fresh insights to spark new ideas. We ’ re a trusted partner to our clients, working behind the scenes to bring imagination, depth, and clarity to their biggest challenges — in entertainment, technology, lifestyle, sports, and gaming. Together, we create with confidence.

We’re proud of our company’s values – these values guide us as we navigate sunny days, gray skies and everything in between:

Do what you love. With conviction.
Where discovery lives. And impact drives.
Celebrate difference. Cultivate belonging.
Big thinking. Collectively inspired.
Embrace the journey. Be human.

The Opportunity

At NRG, we’re always on the lookout for sharp, curious, and creative minds who are excited about diving deep into what makes audiences tick—across entertainment, technology, gaming, sports, lifestyle and beyond.

This posting is for future opportunities across all of our client services teams. We’re always on the hunt for great talent and are excited about the possibility of teaming up in the future. If you’re passionate about qualitative and quantitative research and working with a team that partners with the world’s top brands to shape content, products and strategies that fuel cultural conversations, we want to hear from you!

Below is a snapshot of what a typical Research Analyst role looks like at NRG. The specifics may shift depending on the hiring needs, but this should give you a sense of what we’re about and what we’re looking for. If you don’t hear back for several weeks, don’t worry – we regularly review general applications but prioritize active openings. If there is a potential fit when a position opens, we’ll be in touch!

Your Impact

Support all phases of quantitative and qualitative research projects, including research design, questionnaire and discussion guide development, data analysis and storytelling.
Projects may include methods such as concept evaluation, brand studies, content optimization tests, messaging/positioning evaluation, creative materials tests, market sizing and segmentation.

Help drive quality control processes at each step of the research lifecycle, from checking survey programming logic, questionnaire proofing, number checking and proofing reports and presentations for accuracy.
Partner with internal and external operations teams (programming, fieldwork, facilities, moderators, data processing) to drive projects forward on stringent timelines.
Assist with translating data into clear, actionable insights and recommendations through visual, creative and story-driven reports.

Who We're Looking For

Prior Experience – Prior internship or work experience in market research or consumer insights is preferred. If you are a recent graduate but don’t have relevant work experience, we would love to hear about academic qualitative or quantitative research projects, such as primary survey research, experimental psychology studies, social media analysis, ethnographic research, or any other relevant projects.
Curiosity and Critical Thinking – You are genuinely interested in seeking information on the “whys,” always digging for more information to understand what makes consumers tick. Whether it’s understanding why one marketing message is more effective than another or what consumers think we could be using AI for in the future, you can always find something interesting to sink your teeth into. Simply put, you love to learn.
Clear and Proactive Communicator – You have excellent written and verbal communication skills and are able to communicate clearly and succinctly. You’re comfortable asking questions and sharing your point of view.
Data Driven – You’re comfortable working with data to identify trends and insights, including both structured (i.e. data and hard numbers) and unstructured (i.e. interviews and qualitative) data. Experience visualizing data with tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, Google Docs and Slides is preferred.
Data analysis techniques and software – Familiarity with any of the following data analysis techniques would be awesome: statistical significance testing, correlation analysis, multivariate analysis techniques (such as cluster/segmentation analysis) and conjoint and discrete choice analysis. Experience with statistical packages, like SPSS or Q, are a plus.
Problem Solver – You are a natural problem solver. When something doesn’t go as planned, your first instinct is to look for a solution, rather than viewing it as a roadblock. You’re always on the lookout for new ways to accomplish tasks and have the ability to address issues using creative and collaborative tactics.
Self-starter – Internally-motivated who continuously strives to get things done well, regardless of challenges encountered. You are proactive and always keep an eye on the next step.
Hawk-eyed attention to detail – You notice when font sizes change unexpectedly or a proper noun isn’t capitalized. Errors don’t get past you and you are always focused on ensuring high levels of quality control and reporting.
Expert multitasker – Successfully manages time and multiple competing priorities to ensure deadlines are always met. Staying organized is a must for managing projects!
Great Team Member – T eam player who works collaboratively and harmoniously within a team and across teams. You are comfortable forming connections with colleagues remotely whether that be jumping on a quick video meeting, picking up the phone for a call or chatting with them through IMs. You welcome feedback because you have a zest for learning and growing. You will roll up your sleeves to help get the job done and no task is beneath you.
Your degree(s) – You have a B.A./B.S. degree in areas such as Social Sciences, Psychology, Business, Marketing, Market Research, Statistics, Economics or a r elated field. Additional degrees are welcome!
Passion – A passion or desire to learn about entertainment, technology, gaming, sports and/or lifestyle sectors. You enjoy or are excited by the prospect of staying up to date on industry trends and developments.

Position Type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

What We Offer

We embrace the current era of work and what it means to be a best-in-class employer. We understand the flexibility that is required to recruit and retain incredible talent, whether it’s empowering you to do your best work from the comfort of your home or supporting you if you need to take a mental health day for self-care and rest. Below is a unique blend of benefits tailored to meeting the ever-changing professional landscape.

Flexible/Remote work with optional usage of our great offices in Culver City or New York
Unlimited PTO, volunteer days and a generous number of recharge days including a full office closure during the week of Christmas and New Year’s
Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance Plans
401K with company match
Generous paid Parental Leave
Regular performance evaluations with opportunities for promotions and merit increases
Educational and training reimbursement plan and other training and professional development opportunities
Employee perks program (includes discounts on travel, hotels, cars, fitness, movie tickets and more)
Resources available for mental health, inclusive care and family building
NRGratitude – our company-wide employee recognition program
Regular team/company events and activities including annual summer and holiday parties
Pet friendly headquarters and pet insurance options

Our Commitment

Diversity, equity, and inclusion is at the center of all our practices to ensure that NRG is a place where people from all identities and backgrounds can thrive. NRG is committed to recruiting and retaining diverse talent by supporting their growth through learning programs, internal mobility, affinity group participation and leadership development. Our differences make us a stronger workforce and enhance our creativity and innovation. We are proud to be an inclusive workplace for all and are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by state, federal, or local law.

Compensation

In order to comply with equal pay and salary transparency laws in various locations, we believe the target range of base compensation in all locations within the United States for this role is $62,000 -$70,500. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and location.

jobs.title: Analyste senior des données de jeu / Senior Game Data Analyst
jobs.description:
La division ThunderFire de NetEase Games est un développeur et éditeur de jeux vidéo de premier plan qui s'engage à offrir des expériences de jeu d'exception à un public international. Réparties entre nos studios de Montréal et de Toronto, nos équipes collaborent sur des projets ambitieux et originaux, notamment des titres en cours de développement local, ainsi que des projets internationaux de NetEase tels que Blood Message et Ananta.

L'analyste senior des données de jeu jouera un rôle clé au sein de notre « Insights Center », une équipe pluridisciplinaire qui réunit sous un même toit la recherche sur les utilisateurs de jeux et l'analyse de données. La mission principale de l'Insights Center consiste à tester nos jeux, à recueillir des retours pertinents auprès des joueurs et à combiner les atouts complémentaires de la recherche sur les utilisateurs et de l'analyse de données afin de mettre en lumière les raisons sous-jacentes du comportement des joueurs. Ensemble, nous fournissons à nos équipes de développement et aux parties prenantes du studio des informations exploitables qui influencent la manière dont nos jeux sont conçus.

Le poste

En tant qu'analyste de données de jeu senior, vous transformerez les données des joueurs en récits clairs et convaincants qui guideront des décisions concrètes. Mais l'analyse de données au sein de notre studio va au-delà des rapports automatisés et des tableaux de bord : elle est au cœur d'une analyse exploratoire qui met au jour les facteurs comportementaux et motivationnels qui sous-tendent les actions des joueurs dans nos jeux. Votre travail s'inscrit aux côtés de la recherche utilisateur comme un outil complémentaire lors des tests de jeu et des études sur les joueurs, en apportant des réponses à des questions quantitatives tout en nous aidant à mettre au jour les schémas, les comportements et les attitudes qui définissent l'expérience des joueurs.

Ce poste s'adresse à une personne véritablement curieuse des données et des joueurs, qui raisonne en termes de récits et de perspicacité, et pas seulement de tableaux de bord et de chiffres. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les chercheurs en expérience utilisateur, les concepteurs de jeux, les producteurs et les ingénieurs afin de vous assurer que nous posons les bonnes questions et que nous utilisons les données appropriées pour y répondre.

Il est également important de comprendre comment notre équipe fonctionne au quotidien. Une grande partie de nos efforts est consacrée au développement d'outils internes — de plus en plus alimentés par l'IA — qui aident l'ensemble de l'Insights Center à travailler plus efficacement. Cela signifie que le travail direct sur les données des joueurs n'est pas une activité constante ; il dépend fortement de nos projets en cours, des calendriers de tests de jeu et des besoins du studio. Si la diversité vous passionne, si vous aimez autant créer des outils qu'analyser des données, et si vous souhaitez rester à la pointe des innovations apportées par l'IA dans le domaine de l'analyse, vous vous sentirez comme chez vous ici.

Ce poste est ouvert aux candidats basés à Montréal ou à Toronto. Cela dit, la priorité sera donnée aux candidats basés à Montréal, compte tenu de la concentration de notre équipe d'analyse dans cette ville et des exigences en matière de présence au bureau (actuellement 3 jours par semaine, sous réserve de modification).

Responsabilités

Analyser les données des joueurs afin d'identifier des tendances, des schémas et des enseignements qui éclairent les décisions de conception du jeu et soutiennent les initiatives de recherche sur les utilisateurs, en replaçant toujours vos conclusions dans le contexte plus large du comportement des joueurs.
Élaborer des rapports, des tableaux de bord et des visualisations qui communiquent les enseignements tirés des données de manière claire et convaincante, tant aux parties prenantes techniques que non techniques.
Posséder une connaissance pratique des pipelines de données et de la modélisation des données en amont, suffisante pour traduire les besoins analytiques en exigences techniques, signaler les problèmes de qualité des données et comprendre comment les décisions prises en amont dans le pipeline se répercutent sur la précision en aval – élément clé pour collaborer efficacement avec les ingénieurs en analyse et les ingénieurs de données.
Contribuer au développement et à la maintenance d'outils internes – de plus en plus basés sur l'IA – qui aident à la fois les chercheurs en expérience utilisateur et les analystes à suivre, visualiser et analyser plus efficacement les données issues des tests de jeu.
Collaborer avec les concepteurs de jeux, les développeurs et les chercheurs en expérience utilisateur pour identifier dès le départ les bonnes questions et les besoins en données, puis les accompagner tout au long du cycle de vie complet de l'analyse : vérifier que les données sont bien collectées, définir les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) et les métriques, visualiser les résultats, et mettre en évidence les tendances, les réponses et les nouvelles questions méritant d'être explorées.
Surveiller les métriques et les KPI des jeux afin d'identifier les problèmes potentiels et les opportunités d'amélioration.
Expérimentez de manière proactive les outils et approches d'IA en matière d'analyse, en vous tenant informé des tendances émergentes et en partageant vos connaissances avec l'équipe.
Recherchez des opportunités d'exploiter les données, les outils et les bonnes pratiques afin d'améliorer la qualité et l'efficacité de la fonction d'analyse.
Tenez-vous informé des tendances du secteur et des bonnes pratiques en matière d'analyse des données de jeux vidéo.

Qualifications

Expérience

Licence ou master dans un domaine quantitatif tel que l'intelligence d'affaires, les mathématiques, les statistiques, l'informatique ou une discipline connexe (ou expérience pratique équivalente).
Au moins 5 ans d'expérience en analyse de données, de préférence dans le secteur du jeu vidéo.
Expérience avérée dans la transformation de données comportementales des joueurs en informations et recommandations claires et exploitables.
Expérience de la collaboration avec des partenaires interfonctionnels : concepteurs, développeurs, producteurs et, idéalement, chercheurs en expérience utilisateur.
Une expérience de travail au sein d'équipes internationales et avec des collègues et parties prenantes dont l'anglais n'est pas la langue maternelle est un atout.

Compétences techniques

Solides compétences en SQL et connaissance des outils d'analyse et de manipulation des données.
Expérience pratique de notre pile analytique principale ou d'outils équivalents : Sigma, dbt et Snowflake.
Expérience approfondie des outils de visualisation des données et de BI (Sigma, Tableau, Looker, Power BI ou similaires).
Une expérience en modélisation de données est un atout (modélisation dimensionnelle de Kimball, Data Vault, etc.).
Une expérience avec Python (ou R/équivalent) est un atout.
Connaissance – et, idéalement, expérience pratique – des applications d'IA/ML en analyse de données (LLM pour la génération d'informations, la modélisation prédictive, la détection d'anomalies, etc.).
Une bonne connaissance de l'industrie du jeu vidéo et des cycles de production est un atout.

Atouts supplémentaires

Le bilinguisme français-anglais est un atout pour notre studio de Montréal.
Expérience de collaboration avec des chercheurs en expérience utilisateur (UX).
Expérience de travail avec des équipes de développement de jeux chinoises ou au sein d'un éditeur de jeux chinois.
Connaissance de l'analyse marketing, des données d'acquisition d'utilisateurs ou des canaux de retours de la communauté.

Pourquoi nous pourrions être la compagnie parfaite pour toi:

Nous offrons l'expérience unique de faire partie de la création d'une nouvelle équipe de jeu internationale en plein cœur de Montréal, qui bénéficie de la richesse de la diversité de ses membres et de l'échange culturel avec nos partenaires à Hangzhou.

Nous offrons également :

Couverture d'assurance et télémédecine dès le 1er jour;
Indemnité transports et repas;
Prime de référencement;
REER avec contribution de l'employeur.

Rejoins-nous pour travailler sur un projet ambitieux, dans une atmosphère unique de start-up et avec une équipe de développeurs de jeux passionnés et pleins d'énergie !

Senior Game Data Analyst

ThunderFire Division of NetEase Games is a leading game developer and publisher committed to delivering top-quality gaming experiences to a global audience. Operating across studios in Montreal and Toronto, our teams collaborate on ambitious, original IPs - including titles in active development locally, as well as global NetEase projects such as Blood Message and Ananta.

The Senior Game Data Analyst will be a key contributor within our Insights Center - a multidisciplinary team that brings together Games User Research and Data Analytics under one roof. The Insights Center's core mission is to test our games, gather meaningful feedback from players, and combine the complementary strengths of user research and data analytics to surface the underlying why behind player behaviour. Together, we deliver actionable insights to our game teams and studio stakeholders that shape how our games are built.

The Role

As a Senior Game Data Analyst, you will turn player data into clear, compelling stories that drive real decisions. But analytics in our studio goes beyond automated reporting and dashboarding - it's central to exploratory analysis that uncovers the behavioral and motivational drivers behind what players do in our games. Your work sits alongside user research as a complementary tool in playtests and player studies, answering quantitative questions while helping us uncover the patterns, behaviours, and attitudes that define the player experience.

This is a role for someone genuinely curious about data and about players - someone who thinks in terms of narrative and insight, not just dashboards and numbers. You will partner closely with user researchers, game designers, producers, and engineers to ensure we're asking the right questions and using the right data to answer them.

It's also important to understand how our team works day to day. If you're excited by variety, by building tools as much as analyzing data, and by staying at the cutting edge of how AI is reshaping analytics, you'll feel at home here.

This role is open to candidates based in either Montreal or Toronto. That said, priority will be given to Montreal-based candidates, given the concentration of our analytics team there and expectations of in-office days (current rate at 3 days per week, subject to change).

What You'll Do

Analyze player data to identify trends, patterns, and insights that inform game design decisions and support user research initiatives - always framing your findings as part of the broader story of player behaviour.
Develop reports, dashboards, and visualizations that communicate data insights clearly and persuasively to technical and non-technical stakeholders alike.
Working knowledge of data pipelines and upstream data modeling, sufficient to translate analytical needs into technical requirements, flag data quality issues, and understand how upstream pipeline decisions ripple into downstream accuracy - key to partnering effectively with Analytics Engineers and Data Engineers.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of internal tooling - increasingly AI-powered - that helps both user researchers and analysts track, visualize, and analyze data from playtests more effic

Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI infrastructure company with a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. Our competitive advantage—“Speed is the only moat”—is directly tied to our ability to rapidly design, manufacture, and deploy our own modular power and compute infrastructure.

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to join our R&D organization and drive programs that evaluate and advance the next generation of AI data center technologies. You will manage initiatives that span multiple engineering disciplines—from early-stage technology evaluations and partnerships with emerging startups and industry providers, through pilot-scale validation and production handoff for hyperscale deployment.

Crusoe’s R&D team exists to look around corners: identifying the technologies and design approaches that will define future data center platforms, testing them rigorously, and delivering validated solutions to the engineering teams that build and deploy our infrastructure. As a TPM in his team, you will be the operational backbone of that process—coordinating across R&D, engineering, external technology partners, and leadership to drive programs from concept through pilot to hyperscale readiness.

What You’ll Be Working On:

R&D Program Execution: Own and drive R&D programs end-to-end—from early-stage technology evaluation and partner engagement through pilot-scale deployment and production handoff for hyperscale rollout. Bring structure, rigor, and pace to programs that are inherently exploratory.
Engineering Team Partnership: Serve as R&D’s program interface to engineering teams across the company. Coordinate joint planning, manage shared initiative pipelines, and ensure R&D outputs are aligned with the needs of the teams building and deploying infrastructure.
Technology Evaluation Support: Coordinate the operational aspects of technology evaluations: vendor engagements, test protocols, data collection, success criteria, and structured go/no-go decision frameworks. Ensure evaluations are completed on schedule with clear, documented outcomes.
External Partner Management: Manage relationships with external technology vendors, emerging startups, design firms, and development partners engaged in R&D programs. Own scope definition, deliverable quality, schedule accountability, contracts, and commercial terms. Help coordinate joint evaluations and pilot programs with industry and research partners.
Cross-Functional Coordination: Drive alignment across R&D, engineering, operations, and leadership stakeholders. Translate technical complexity into clear program milestones, risk registers, and decision points that enable rapid execution.
Program Reporting: Maintain program status visibility through regular reporting to R&D leadership and engineering stakeholders. Proactively identify and escalate risks and blockers.
Technical Documentation: Ensure R&D programs produce comprehensive documentation—including technical assessments, pilot results, vendor evaluations, and production handoff packages—that enable engineering teams to adopt and scale R&D-validated solutions.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

Experience: 7+ years of progressive experience in technical program management, project management, or systems engineering, with a meaningful portion in data center infrastructure, manufacturing, or related industrial environments.
Technical Background: Engineering degree or equivalent technical foundation. You started your career as an engineer and transitioned into program management—you bring genuine technical fluency to every conversation, not just process discipline.
Data Center Knowledge: Working familiarity with data center infrastructure—power distribution, cooling systems, facility design, or compute/networking. You can engage credibly with engineers across these domains and ask the right questions.
Program Execution: Demonstrated track record of delivering complex, cross-functional programs on time. Comfortable managing ambiguity, competing priorities, and multiple concurrent workstreams.
Vendor Management: Experience managing external vendors, contractors, or design partners including contract negotiation, scope management, and delivery accountability.
Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to translate technical program details into clear executive summaries and to facilitate productive discussions across diverse engineering disciplines.

Direct experience in data center construction, commissioning, or operations.
Background in manufacturing environments, particularly modular or containerized systems.

jobs.description:
How you move is why we’re here. ®

Now more than ever.

Get back to what you need and love to do.

The possibilities are endless...

Now more than ever, our guiding principles are helping us in our search for exceptional talent - candidates who align with our unique workplace culture and who want to maximize the abundant opportunities for growth and success.

If this describes you then let’s talk!

HSS is consistently among the top-ranked hospitals for orthopedics and rheumatology by U.S. News & World Report. As a recipient of the Magnet Award for Nursing Excellence, HSS was the first hospital in New York City to receive the distinguished designation. Whether you are early in your career or an expert in your field, you will find HSS an innovative, supportive and inclusive environment.

Working with colleagues who love what they do and are deeply committed to our Mission, you too can be part of our transformation across the enterprise.

Emp Status

Regular Full time

Work Shift

Day (United States of America)

Compensation Range

The base pay scale for this position is $88,500.00 - $134,750.00. In addition, this position will be eligible for additional benefits consistent with the role. The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be determined based on various factors, including but not limited to: scope of role, level of experience, education, accomplishments, internal equity, budget, and subject to Fair Market Value evaluation. The hiring range listed is a good faith determination of potential compensation at the time of this job advertisement and may be modified in the future.

What You Will Be Doing

The Project Manager is responsible for the end-to-end delivery of large-scale healthcare technology projects associated with new construction, facility activations, renovations, practice expansions, and enterprise technology initiatives. This role oversees all phases of project execution including planning, budgeting, procurement, supply chain management, infrastructure deployment, application readiness, operational readiness, go-live activation, and stabilization support.

The Project Manager coordinates the deployment of physical technology infrastructure, end-user computing devices, network and telecommunications systems, audiovisual systems, security technologies, and clinical applications. In addition, the role is responsible for overseeing the implementation and activation of electronic medical record (EMR) and clinical systems, ensuring operational, technical, and application workstreams remain synchronized throughout the project lifecycle.

This role serves as the primary point of accountability between Information Technology, Clinical Operations, Facilities, Design & Construction, Finance, Vendors, Application Teams, and Executive Leadership to ensure technology and operational readiness milestones are successfully achieved.

Who Will Love This Job

An organizer who will keep multiple projects running on time and budget while balancing competing tasks for yourself and others.
A strategist who will assist in project planning and execution. Understanding key goals and satisfying a diverse group of stakeholders and their priorities.
An adapter who is comfortable working as part of a team-based portfolio and supporting other’s work-styles and requests for custom materials.
A collaborator who will liaise and coordinate across the organization and be a primary point of contact for internal and vendor team members.
A proud evangelist who will advocate project management principles, and the ability to transfer that knowledge to HSS staff and end-users through the creation of best-practice materials.
A communicator and presenter who will effectively provide concise status updates on all projects and represent the team in management venues.

What You’ll Do

Be a project manager as a part of the IT Portfolio Office, reporting to the Director of Strategic Growth, to support Enterprise strategic initiatives within the Technology Department’s Portfolio. Specifically, the Strategic Growth portfolio support new construction, renovations, relocations, and physician onboarding
Have a deep understanding of workflows and hospital operations to be a strategic partner to the wider business, acting as the primary interface between IT, Informatics, and Operations.
Ensure organizational alignment with the Enterprise PMO across cross-portfolio objectives and advising hospital leaders.
Create and maintain project tools and processes based on best practices for cross-team use: project plans, issue and enhancement trackers, training companions, agenda templates, executive engagement/escalation, change management, etc.
Develop and maintain project management training for the department, including consultative services.
Strategize and oversee the development, implementation, and maintenance lifecycles of multiple projects simultaneously, including:
Plan and Execute:
Understand design documents, construction drawings, technology standards, and infrastructure requirements to influence project plans.
Develop and manage capital and operating budgets for strategic growth projects, tracking project expenditures, purchase orders, contracts, invoices, and change orders.
Coordinate procurement activities for infrastructure, telecommunications, end-user devices, audiovisual systems, clinical technologies, and software solutions.
Facilitate the completion of project scope/resource requirements, project charter, and lessons learned documentation.
Define and tracking all tasks, milestones, and deliverables.
Manage project deadlines and hold the team accountable for deliverables, including software/integrations (Epic EMR), hardware, network infrastructure, telecommunications, etc.
Oversee conversion of provider schedules, appointment templates, and patient access workflows necessary to support new locations or operational transitions.
Partner with clinical, operational, training, and application teams to ensure workflow readiness and adoption.
Assist staff with research, meeting scheduling and facilitating, note taking/follow up, and general team coordination.
Take ownership of issues and the delivery of resolutions. Track all issues and risks with the appropriate tools.
Monitor and track all projects with the appropriate tools, and report statuses regularly to stakeholder groups.
Validate designed and standardized deployments against stakeholder expectations and facilitate signoff on final deployment plan, including any updates and revisions needed to other related groups such as construction, planning, budget, or other impacted groups.
Coordinate structured cabling, MDF/IDF buildout activities, technology room readiness, and infrastructure commissioning.
Lead all testing events and Operational/Technical sign off, including, but not limited to Unit, Integrated, Device, Technical and Workflow Dress Rehearsals, etc.
Oversee appointment conversion, cutover planning, assist with communication on application-specific steps related to new facility activation and moves
Coordinate technology staging, imaging, asset management, deployment, installation, and production cutover activities.
Manage command center planning, onsite support, and issue escalation processes. Coordinate go-live staffing schedule, coverage, and stabilization.
Develop plan and ensure completion of technology, operational, and clinical readiness checkpoints prior to activation.
Learn and Grow:
Research new methods for enhancing performance, and track project interventions with positive outcomes.
Complete project assessments to innovate new processes and tools for the organization. Particular ownership of technology standards documentation development and maintenance.

Qualifications

A bachelor’s degree at a 4-year institution; preferred majors in computer science, business, or healthcare.
At least 5 years of experience working as a Project/Program/Portfolio Manager in a high intensity environment; healthcare and Epic experience preferred.
Demonstrated ability to manage and work well in a team, navigate complicated governance structures, remove roadblocks for team members, and adapt to a constantly changing healthcare environment with competing priorities.
Proven comfort with strategic planning/capital planning, procurement, risk management, conflict resolution, and change management.
Experience in healthcare construction, ambulatory center activations, facility relocations, and/or renovations. Expertise in EMR Implementations and their associated activities.
Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written skills; collaborative; assertive; strategic and tactful.
Advanced knowledge of the Microsoft suite of products.
Expertise in project management software (i.e., Jira, Monday.com, Smartsheet) and working knowledge of Lean/Agile practices preferred.
Willingness to work a flexible schedule according to business requirements.

The Ideal Candidate Will Have

Epic implementation or activation experience with direct support of Operational Dress Rehearsals (ODRs), Technical Dress Rehearsals (TDRs), Facility Activations, Occupancy Readiness Assessments, Command Center Operations, Ambulatory Practice Openings
PMP, PgMP, PfMP, PMI-ACP, DASSM, CSM, SAFe Agilist certifications preferred.
Experience with OKRs preferred.

Significant impact on a function and/or the business through making decisions that determine technical approaches and strategies for the area.

Provide coaching and development to RDs and WGEs on best practices for attracting and converting top advisor talent.
Conduct cyclical training sessions on market trends, competitor intelligence, and recruiting strategies.

Excellent communication skills and interpersonal relationships with ability to influence and negotiate with stakeholders.
Advanced judgment and analytical skills to solve problems and develop innovative solutions.
Ability to think beyond existing solutions and assumptions.
