new_jobs.description:
Job Description

WSP is seeking EHV EPC Project Manager (Power Delivery)- Remote
for our Power & Energy Program Management Office in Portland, OR.
The following locations will also be considered: Los Angeles, CA, San Francisco, CA, San Diego, CA, Seattle, WA, Boise, ID, Helena, MT and Phoenix, AZ.
In this position, you will be responsible for cradle-to-grave execution of high-voltage transmission EPC projects, from project development and design through construction, energization, and final closeout.

This Opportunity

This position provides high level technical project leadership, and guidance with managing the administrative, commercial, and technical components of EHV Transmission and Substation project(s) or portfolio of projects in accordance with WSP’s core values, and the level of project services agreed upon in the contract by WSP and the client(s).

Responsible for the overall performance of assigned project(s) that are moderate and larger size/complexity and regional in scope, and includes oversight for financial, technical, client satisfaction, quality, safety, and schedule.

Ensures that responsibilities throughout the project lifecycle (proposal phase, project startup and planning, project execution, reporting, and project closeout) are adhered to, delivered, and audited with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable corporate standards for safety, execution, profitability, and operational purpose.

Your Impact

Coordinate and communicate with all levels of management and disciplines throughout the project life cycle to support project cost and schedule objectives, both internally and within the client’s systems.
Lead the development of project proposals, cost estimates, scope, schedules, and resource plans
Oversee management of budgeting, forecasting, scheduling, cost and change management and control.
Provide regular project reporting and updates to clients, technical leads, and business leaders, identifying any emergent issues with scope, risk, and/or budget and mitigation strategies.
Be the face of WSP for the client. Develop and nurture strong, long-term relationships with client by understanding their needs, providing tailored solutions, and ensuring consistent communication to drive satisfaction and retention.
Adherence to proven processes and ability to develop new processes to standardize procedures.
Adhere to safety regulations and enforce project safety standards
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree (Electrical, Civil, Mechanical, Project Management or Construction Management), Engineering Technology, Physical Sciences, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience within an A/E/C firm, utility, EPC, or power delivery consulting environment.
10+ years of relevant post education experience in a project management role within our industry.
3+ years of EHV transmission level voltage project experience (115kV up to 500kV)
Cradle to grave EPC project management experience for transmission level voltage
Highly proficient understanding of project delivery process and strong background and experience in project management. Experience managing projects through a variety of delivery models (DBB, EPC, PDB).
Advanced proficiency with analytical and organizational skills, with business acumen to bridge the business and project management.
Advanced proficiency with interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively, persuasively, and tactfully with leadership, subcontractors, and employees at all levels of the organization.
Excellent self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and adjusting readily to the changing prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
Works independently and provides guidance and leadership to mid-level to senior level team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
Advanced proficiency with technical writing, office automation, relevant software, MS Office suite products (e.g., Word, Excel, Visio, Project, SharePoint), technology, spreadsheets, and PM tools.
Ability to elicit cooperation from a wide variety of sources, including senior management, subcontractors, consultants, and company-wide staff, including those with whom no formal hierarchical relationship exits.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Strong ability to quickly adapt to change and demonstrate flexibility to a variety of schedules and hours to meet project-specific needs.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.

WSP Benefits

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation

Expected Salary (all locations): $120,000 - $210,000

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

WSP provides a flexible and agile workplace model while meeting client needs. Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

new_jobs.title: Microelectronics - Program Manager - Business Execution
new_jobs.description:
Aquatech’s Microelectronics business is entering a period of rapid global growth. Microelectronics Program Manager - Business Execution & Integration will support execution of the Microelectronics global strategy by establishing the structure, coordination, reporting, and accountability required to convert business priorities into completed actions and measurable results.

The role serves as an internal execution and organizational integrator, working across engineering, technology, project execution, commercial, supply chain, finance, HR, regional teams, and other Aquatech organizations. The Program Manager will coordinate cross-functional initiatives, develop and maintain implementation schedules, establish reporting and KPIs, manage organizational interfaces and stakeholder agreements, track commitments, and drive follow-through.

A significant emphasis of the position is working effectively within Aquatech’s matrix organization. The Program Manager will establish clear working agreements with internal and partner organizations regarding scope, responsibilities, resources, interfaces, deliverables, schedules, governance, and reporting. Success depends on creating organizational accountability and achieving results through coordination and influence rather than direct authority.

This is not a customer project-management or PMO position. Project managers and functional organizations retain accountability for customer projects and technical deliverables. This role applies program- and project-management discipline primarily to internal Microelectronics organizational, strategic, standardization, product-development, and business-improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Business Operating Rhythm & Accountability

Establish and maintain the Microelectronics operating cadence, dashboards, KPIs, action tracking, decision logs, business reviews, and reporting processes required to provide clear visibility into priorities, commitments, accountable owners, milestones, risks, resource requirements, and completion status.

Internal Program & Initiative Execution

Convert Microelectronics priorities into executable internal programs with defined scope, owners, schedules, milestones, dependencies, resources, KPIs, and completion criteria; coordinate implementation across functions and organizations while functional and technical teams retain ownership of their respective technical scope and deliverables.

Internal initiatives may include organizational integration, global execution-model implementation, engineering and execution standardization, product development and productization, process improvements, business systems, supplier strategies, and organizational or cultural change.

Global Strategy Execution & Organizational Infrastructure

Translate the Microelectronics global strategy into practical organizational actions by coordinating roles and responsibilities, decision rights, resource requirements, operating processes, governance, standardization, organizational interfaces, and implementation activities required to support global execution and continued growth.

Matrix Organization & Stakeholder Management

Develop and maintain effective working agreements across Microelectronics and partner Aquatech organizations, defining scope boundaries, responsibilities, shared resources, interfaces, deliverables, schedules, communication requirements, governance, reporting, and escalation paths while tracking commitments and reinforcing organizational accountability.

Initial Priorities

During The First Six Months, The Program Manager Should

Implement the Microelectronics Global Execution Model

Drive implementation and organizational adoption of the Microelectronics Global Execution Model by converting the defined strategy into a structured implementation program with clear organizational responsibilities, schedules, milestones, dependencies, governance, decision rights, KPIs, and completion criteria.

Maintain the integrated implementation schedule; coordinate activities across Microelectronics and partner Aquatech organizations; establish required stakeholder agreements; track commitments and dependencies; identify resource constraints and implementation barriers; facilitate resolution and escalation; and drive completion of actions required to embed the model into normal business operations.

Establish the Microelectronics Operating & Reporting Cadence

Implement a consistent business operating rhythm with defined reviews, reporting requirements, dashboards, KPIs, action tracking, decision tracking, and follow-through.

Establish practical mechanisms for measuring progress against business priorities and internal initiatives and for identifying overdue actions, resource constraints, dependencies, and issues requiring resolution.

Establish Organizational Interfaces, Governance & Accountability

Document and implement the working infrastructure required to operate effectively across the Microelectronics matrix organization and partner Aquatech organizations.

Define and maintain organizational interfaces, scope boundaries, stakeholder agreements, roles and responsibilities, decision rights, shared-resource expectations, communication requirements, governance, reporting, and escalation paths.

Develop practical dashboards and KPIs to provide visibility into implementation progress, organizational commitments, resource requirements, business performance, and critical risks. Track agreed actions and deliverables to completion and reinforce accountability across participating organizations.

Required Experience & Capabilities

Significant experience in program management, business operations, engineering, organizational transformation, or similar cross-functional execution roles.
Demonstrated ability to convert strategy and broad organizational objectives into structured implementation plans, schedules, milestones, owners, KPIs, and measurable results.
Strong program- and project-management discipline applied to internal organizational and business initiatives.
Experience developing dashboards, KPIs, reporting systems, governance processes, and management routines.
Strong business and financial understanding with the ability to organize and communicate business-performance information.
Demonstrated experience working in complex matrix organizations and coordinating work across functions, regions, and partner organizations.
Ability to establish clear stakeholder agreements regarding scope, responsibilities, interfaces, resources, schedules, deliverables, and accountability.
Strong organizational and analytical skills with disciplined action tracking and follow-through.
Ability to influence teams and reinforce accountability without direct reporting authority.
Clear, concise communication skills with the ability to organize complex issues into actionable information.
High degree of integrity, discretion, urgency, and sound judgment.

Preferred Experience

Experience in semiconductor, microelectronics, water treatment, industrial technology, engineering, construction, or capital-equipment businesses is preferred. Familiarity with ultrapure water, industrial wastewater treatment, water reuse, zero-liquid discharge, or semiconductor infrastructure is beneficial.

Experience implementing global operating models, coordinating geographically distributed organizations, developing internal standards and processes, or executing cross-functional organizational change is highly desirable.

Behaviors

Execution Focused – Converts strategy, plans, and decisions into structured actions and follows them through to completion.

Accountable – Establishes clear ownership, due dates, deliverables, and expectations and consistently tracks commitments.

Structured & Organized – Uses schedules, dashboards, KPIs, action registers, governance, and reporting to create visibility and maintain progress.

Collaborative & Influential – Works effectively across a matrix organization and obtains commitments from teams and partner organizations without relying on formal authority.

Fact Based – Uses data, KPIs, schedules, and documented commitments to identify issues and communicate status objectively.

Persistent – Maintains follow-through across functions and organizations and does not allow actions, decisions, or commitments to stall.

Practical – Focuses on implementation, removing organizational barriers, and creating processes that improve execution rather than adding unnecessary administrative complexity.

Adaptable – Adjusts priorities, schedules, and coordination as business conditions and organizational requirements change.

Reporting & Governance

Microelectronics Program Manager - Business Execution & Integration will report to the Vice Presidents of the Microelectronics Business Unit, with one VP designated as the primary day-to-day sponsor and performance-review owner.

The position is expected to operate primarily as an individual contributor working across a matrix organization. Functional, regional, engineering, project, and account organizations retain accountability for their respective scope and deliverables.

The Program Manager does not lead the Microelectronics PMO or assume responsibility for individual customer projects. The role provides the internal program-management structure, coordination, schedules, reporting, KPIs, stakeholder alignment, governance, and accountability mechanisms required to execute the Microelectronics global strategy and internal organizational initiatives.

Benefits

Aquatech offers a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, company-paid holidays, and a 401K plan (all benefits are based on eligibility).

Essential Functions

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed above and below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Physical Job Demands

Lifting/carrying/moving and exerting up to 50 lbs. of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects, including the human body. May need to climb ladders, cannot be afraid of heights, and will need to wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) while on site. It involves sitting at a desk for extended periods. Needs a high degree of concentration in a busy area.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Civil, or related discipline).

Job Description

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.

The Role

Advanced Vehicle Development is seeking an experienced Technical Project Manager to establish and operate a common work-management approach across program and project teams. This role will configure and administer Jira, develop work breakdown structure templates for different team types, facilitate effective Scrum execution, connect interdependent work across organizations, and create clear status views for executives, leaders, and delivery teams.

The successful candidate will help Advanced Vehicle Development improve execution visibility, cross-functional alignment, and delivery discipline while enabling teams to focus on the work required to advance vehicle architecture and technology development.

What You’ll Do (Responsibilities)

Establish and maintain Jira as a work-management solution for Advanced Vehicle Development program and project teams.
Define Jira workflows, issue types, fields, permissions, naming conventions, and operating guidelines that support consistent execution and reporting.
Create reusable work breakdown structure templates for different Advanced Vehicle Development team types, including program teams and technical project teams.
Translate program milestones and deliverables into appropriately structured epics, features, tasks, dependencies, and actionable work items.

Plan, facilitate, and continuously improve Scrum events, including planning, daily coordination, reviews, retrospectives, and backlog refinement.
Customize Scrum cadences, ceremonies, workflows, and reporting practices to fit the needs of specific team types while maintaining common program-level standards.
Partner with Scrum Managers, project managers, technical leads, and portfolio stakeholders across other organizations to connect related projects, dependencies, milestones, and deliverables.

Establish and maintain mechanisms for identifying, tracking, escalating, and resolving cross-organizational risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies.
Create and maintain multiple Jira dashboards and status views that provide the right level of information for each audience:
Executive View – overall health, major milestones, critical risks, decisions, and delivery confidence.
Leadership View – program progress, cross-team dependencies, capacity concerns, risks, and upcoming commitments.
Team View – backlog health, sprint progress, impediments, assigned work, and near-term priorities.

Define standard status metrics and reporting practices so that project information is timely, consistent, and decision-ready.

Coach teams on practical work-management, backlog-management, estimation, prioritization, and status-reporting practices.
Monitor adoption of the Advanced Vehicle Development work-management approach and identify opportunities to simplify processes and improve execution efficiency.
Develop concise leadership communications, operating reviews, training materials, and user guidance for Jira and related delivery practices.
Work with information technology and enterprise tool teams to address Jira integrations, access, data quality, automation, and reporting needs.

Protect confidential company information and follow applicable General Motors policies and procedures.

2+ years of experience in technical project management, program management, engineering operations, product development, or a related delivery environment.
Demonstrated experience organizing complex, cross-functional work into actionable plans, milestones, deliverables, and dependencies.
Experience facilitating project execution across multiple teams or organizations without direct authority.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to convert complex technical and organizational information into clear status, decisions, actions, and executive-level recommendations.
Strong analytical, planning, prioritization, problem-solving, and follow-through skills.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and adapt to changing program needs.

Experience configuring, administering, or scaling Jira or a comparable work-management platform.
Experience with Scrum, Agile, Kanban, or other iterative delivery methods.
Experience creating work breakdown structures, delivery templates, project taxonomies, or portfolio-management standards.
Experience designing executive, leadership, and team dashboards using Jira or business-intelligence/reporting tools.
Experience connecting dependencies and integrated schedules across engineering, software, product, information technology, or other technical organizations.
Experience supporting vehicle development, advanced engineering, systems engineering, model-based systems engineering, or other complex product-development environments.
Jira, Scrum, Agile, or project-management certification.
Experience with workflow automation, dashboard design, data quality, or tool integration.
Demonstrated ability to build collaboration, influence adoption, and foster a culture of transparency and accountability.

Meet The Team

Splunk, a Cisco company, is building a safer and more resilient digital world with an end-to-end full stack platform made for a hybrid, multi-cloud world. Leading enterprises use our unified security and observability platform to keep their digital systems secure and reliable. Come help organizations be their best, while you reach new heights with a team that has your back!

Your Impact

Leads strategic and operational programs that advance renewals performance, drive recurring revenue growth, and improve customer retention across Splunk and Cisco. Translates business strategy into actionable program roadmaps, aligning cross-functional teams around shared priorities, measurable outcomes, and scalable execution. Leverages data, analytics, and AI-enabled insights to improve forecasting, identify renewal risks and opportunities, optimize processes, and inform strategic decision-making. Experience in software renewals, SaaS subscription management, customer retention, or recurring revenue business models.

new_jobs.title: Sales Enablement Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.
The Role
We’re looking for a proactive and highly organized Sales Enablement Program Manager to help drive clarity, consistency, and continuous learning across Block’s global sales and Account Management teams. You’ll play a critical role in operationalizing our everboarding strategy—ongoing education beyond onboarding. This role requires a strong blend of content operations, learning science, stakeholder management, and sales context awareness.
You Will
Support ongoing learning initiatives by helping to plan, build, facilitate, and maintain scalable sales enablement content beyond onboarding.
Curate and maintain centralized knowledge resources, partnering with subject matter experts (SMEs) across Product, Marketing, and Sales to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Help operationalize the everboarding strategy, coordinating timelines, deliverables, and stakeholder communications.
Organize and update internal learning assets, ensuring documentation is easy to find, up-to-date, and aligned with sales priorities.
Manage internal communications related to enablement, such as newsletters, training calendars, training decks, and update broadcasts to reduce noise and increase clarity.
Collect feedback and track program impact, using data to assess adoption, knowledge retention, and performance improvements.
Support regional Canada enablement needs, ensuring content is localized and relevant for diverse sales teams across markets.
Promote knowledge-sharing practices, including documenting playbooks, building FAQs, and contributing to internal wikis or LMS content.

You Have

4+ years of experience in Sales Enablement, Sales, or Account Management.
Strong understanding of adult learning theories and experience applying them to training design, content delivery, or knowledge-sharing systems.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with an ability to influence and collaborate across functions and levels.
Proven ability to prioritize effectively, manage competing demands, and maintain clarity under ambiguity.

Nice to Have
Background in instructional design, content strategy, or sales operations.
Exposure to coaching methodologies such as GROW to support learner development and behavior change.

who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

Strategic Fulfilment Programs is the team that bridges strategy and execution across Global Fulfilment. We align priorities, investments, and resources to ensure the right initiatives are delivered at the right time, creating sustainable value for our business, distribution network, stores, and guests in North America, EMEA, APAC and China

Core Responsibilities

Lead the end-to-end planning and execution of DC and logistics projects; develop detailed project plans, set milestones, and ensure alignment with regional and global logistics objectives.

Managing fulfilment programs and projects from planning to operations. Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including operations, IT, finance, and procurement, to ensure successful project delivery

Identify and mitigate risks associated with multi-carrier logistics operations, including delays, capacity issues, and regulatory compliance challenges.

Value Add

Work with global and regional teams to ensure consistency in the multi-carrier programs in North America, EMEA, APAC and China; sharing best practices and lessons learned.
Experience with 3rd party logistics organizations and project management

7-10 years of Project or Program management experience.

Strong understanding of the EMEA supply chain landscape, including regulatory requirements and carrier networks.

Lead with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.

Reviews employees performance and recommends employee compensation; coaches for improved performance and disciplines as necessary. Interacts directly with subordinates and peer groups. Builds strong internal and external relationships that require exchanging of information and providing explanations in a problem solving capacity.

Performs tasks such as, but not limited to, the following:

NPI & Account Management: Acts as the primary interface and relationship manager between key customer leadership and internal operational teams, specifically overseeing high-complexity NPI and managing large-scale, strategic account portfolios.
Project Planning & Execution: Develops, implements, and executes flawless end-to-end program/project plans across all phases of the product lifecycle.

Stakeholder Communication: Establishes and leads regular program tracking meetings, providing transparent status reporting and executive updates for monthly Operations Reviews and quarterly Customer Performance Reviews.

In-depth understanding of the semiconductor industry, specifically manufacturing complex electromechanical assemblies and supply chain management (SCM) dynamics.
Ability to align cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders without direct reporting authority.
Demonstrated methodologies for proactive risk identification, mitigation, and navigating fluctuating timelines and dynamic scopes.
Deep knowledge of product pricing, business risks, contract negotiation, and margin structures (Value-Add & Materials).
Strong verbal, written, and presentation skills with the ability to articulate technical and project details clearly to executives and customers.

10+ years of relevant project/program management experience overseeing complex electromechanical assemblies within the semiconductor industry.

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical/engineering discipline.
Certifications: PMP (Project Management Professional) or equivalent PM certification preferred.

Duties of this position are performed in a normal office environment.
Duties may require extended periods of sitting and sustained visual concentration on a computer monitor or on numbers and other detailed data.
Repetitive manual movements (e.g., data entry, using a computer mouse, using a calculator, etc.) are frequently required.
Above demands are carried out within the local existing Health and Safety guidelines

Description

Senior Project Manager

Drive Execution. Remove Roadblocks. Deliver Predictable Outcomes.

At Power Integrations, we develop innovative semiconductor technologies that power energy-efficient solutions used around the world. From consumer electronics and industrial applications to electric vehicles and renewable energy systems, our products help customers solve increasingly complex power conversion challenges.

We're looking for a seasoned Senior Project Manager who thrives at the intersection of technology, execution, and leadership. This is not a project coordinator role. It's an opportunity for an experienced execution leader to become a trusted partner to Business Unit and Engineering leadership, helping our teams bring innovative semiconductor products from concept to production with greater speed, transparency, and predictability.

If you're energized by driving complex projects, influencing across organizations, and helping teams make better decisions faster, we'd love to talk with you.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Project Manager, you will lead the execution of complex semiconductor product development projects across multiple functions and geographies.

You'll serve as the organization's independent view of execution, partnering closely with Business Unit leaders, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Applications, Packaging, and Test teams to ensure projects stay aligned, risks are surfaced early, decisions happen quickly, and commitments are met.

This Role Is Built Around a Clear Operating Model

Business Unit Leaders own product strategy, portfolio priorities, and business outcomes.
Functional Leaders own technical solutions and execution within their teams.
You own integrated project execution, cross-functional alignment, schedule predictability, dependency management, and delivery transparency.

Success in this role requires more than maintaining schedules. You'll anticipate issues before they become problems, identify resource constraints before they affect commitments, and help leadership teams make informed decisions that keep projects moving forward.

What You'll Do

Lead Complex Product Development Projects

Drive cross-functional semiconductor product development projects from concept through production release.
Build and maintain integrated project plans, schedules, milestones, and critical-path activities.
Ensure alignment across Engineering, Applications, Packaging, Test, Quality, Operations, Marketing, and Business Unit stakeholders.
Establish clear project objectives, deliverables, dependencies, and success metrics.
Drive accountability and execution across matrixed teams.

Manage the Critical Path

Own and actively manage integrated project schedules.
Identify bottlenecks, competing priorities, and resource constraints before they impact commitments.
Anticipate and address dependencies across multiple organizations and development phases.
Develop recovery plans when projects deviate from schedule expectations.
Maintain clear visibility into execution readiness and milestone achievement.

Enable Better Decisions

Facilitate discussions that drive timely, data-based decisions.
Clarify ownership and ensure actions are completed.
Escalate issues appropriately and proactively.
Help leadership understand tradeoffs, risks, and schedule impacts.
Create transparency and eliminate surprises.

Drive Cross-Functional Alignment

Serve as the central coordination point across technical and business functions.
Build strong partnerships while maintaining objective project oversight.
Resolve conflicts and remove barriers to progress.
Ensure organizational priorities are translated into executable plans.

Proactively Manage Risk

Identify execution risks early and assess potential impacts.
Drive mitigation planning and accountability.
Monitor project health, resource availability, and milestone readiness.
Surface issues before they become critical delays.
Provide leadership with a clear view of risks and opportunities.

Leverage Technology and AI

Utilize modern project management tools, analytics, and dashboards to improve visibility and predictability.
Apply AI-enabled solutions to automate status gathering, action tracking, reporting, and risk identification.
Use data and automation to reduce administrative work and focus on execution leadership.
Help advance scalable project management practices across the organization.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Operations, or a related field.
8+ years of project management experience in semiconductor, electronics, hardware, or other complex product development environment.
Demonstrated success leading large, cross-functional technical projects.
Strong understanding of semiconductor development lifecycles, including:

IC development and tapeout
Validation
Package development
Test development
Qualification
Manufacturing readiness
Production release
Experience managing critical paths, dependencies, resource constraints, and project risks.
Strong leadership and influencing skills within matrix organizations.
Exceptional communication and executive presentation capabilities.
Proven ability to drive accountability without direct authority.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a related field.
PMP, PgMP, Agile, or similar project management certification.
Experience leading global semiconductor development teams.
Familiarity with PLM, ERP, and portfolio management systems.
Experience implementing AI-enabled project management or workflow automation solutions.

What Success Looks Like

Within This Role, You Will

Become the organization's trusted source of execution transparency.
Deliver projects with greater predictability and fewer surprises.
Identify risks and resource challenges early enough to avoid missed commitments.
Accelerate decision-making through structured communication and thoughtful escalation.
Strengthen accountability across teams and functions.
Enable business and technical leaders to focus on strategy and innovation while you ensure execution stays on track.
Help Power Integrations continuously improve how complex product development projects are planned and delivered.

Why Power Integrations?

At Power Integrations, you'll work on technologies that make electronic devices and energy systems more efficient worldwide. You'll collaborate with talented engineers, business leaders, and operations teams while influencing projects that have a direct impact on our customers and our business.

This is a highly visible role with significant opportunity to shape execution excellence across the organization and help deliver the next generation of industry-leading semiconductor product.

If you're passionate about driving clarity, alignment, accountability, and execution in a complex technical environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Power Integrations is committed to building teams that drive innovation and therefore review a range of factors when determining compensation. The annual base pay range for this position is $187,000 and $260,000. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, qualifications and work location.

The range displayed on the job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for this position in California. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Power Integrations also offers to our eligible employees a comprehensive total rewards package that includes equity, medical benefits, ESPP, 401K, tuition reimbursement and time off programs. For additional benefits, please visit https://www.power.com/company/our-sustainability-priorities/people-our-engine-innovation

Together, we act as a single-source provider, deploying cooling technologies as scalable systems optimized for efficiency, spatial constraints, and overall performance. At Gradian, you'll work alongside others who get genuinely fired up by complex problems, see your work go from first sketch to job site in weeks, not years, and know that while we're developing the technologies critical for AI infrastructure to scale, our culture remains people-first by design.

Coordinate resource allocation across project teams; surface resource conflicts and work with functional managers to resolve them

PMP (Project Management Professional) certification or equivalent formal project management education (e.g., a degree program with a concentration in project or program management), or equivalent relevant experience

Demonstrated proficiency with project scheduling tools (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent)
Strong understanding of stage-gate product development processes
Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills

Preferred

Experience in HVAC, thermal management, or related mechanical systems industries
Familiarity with liquid cooling architectures and equipment for data center and high-density applications (e.g., CDUs, rear door heat exchangers) and fluid-side heat transfer principles
Experience working within or alongside a PMO structure
Background in design-for-manufacturability (DFM) or design-for-quality (DFQ) methodologies
Proficiency with PLM or ERP systems
Six Sigma or Lean certification

Key Competencies

Ability to engage meaningfully with engineering teams on product design, testing, and performance trade-offs
Strong sense of ownership; bias toward action and on-time delivery
Ability to manage complexity, prioritize competing demands, and keep projects organized under ambiguity
Skilled at leading cross-functional teams without direct authority
Clear and concise communicator, both written and verbal, able to tailor messages to technical and executive audiences alike
Continuously seeks to improve processes, tools, and team effectiveness

new_jobs.title: Deputy Program Manager for Security & Protection - Active Clearance Required
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We have an opening for a Deputy Program Manager
(DPM) for the Security and Protection (S&P) Program within the Security Organization (SO). The S&P DPM is responsible for general oversight and personnel management of all S&P sections; in research and development (R&D), manufacturing, quality and assurance (QA), order compliance, systems and equipment distribution, as well as viability and operations in support of high-end security systems and associated technologies. In this position you will manage a multi-disciplinary team of scientists, software programmers, engineering/ technical staff, quality assurance, and administrative personnel, while being responsible for all areas of program management, high-level goal setting, and the development of strategies.

You will be responsible for assisting with the execution of the program’s annual operating plan (AOP) to meet objectives and deliverables by the NNSA Office of Defense Nuclear Security (NA-70), as well as Strategic Partnership Programs. This position is in the National Security Engineering Division (NSED) within the Engineering Directorate.

Depending on your assignment, this position may offer a hybrid work arrangement, blending in-person and virtual presence. You may have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.

This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level.

You will

Provide leadership and technical oversight to the multi-disciplinary team including matrixed full-time employees (FTE’s) from directorates throughout the laboratory, as well as contractors.
Manage cross-sectional (Software Development, IT Management, Systems Engineering, and Enterprise Communications) projects and logistical workflow.
Provide leadership and managerial oversight S&P’s Annual Operating Plan (AOP), including the allocation, monitoring of available personnel, and a ~$30M-$40M dollar budget.
Provide oversight and guidance of S&P’s annual operating budget and effort.
Lead recruiting, hiring, mentoring and the development of high-quality staff to support program sections and assist in their professional growth and advancement in technical and security areas.
Participate in NA-70/713 enterprise collaborative meetings and ensure S&P’s scope of work is clearly defined and advocate for and support development of appropriately funded scope. Effectively interface with other national laboratories and industry partners as part of the collaboration team.
Establish relationships with Department of Energy (DOE) enterprise sites security managers, system owners, personnel, and federal office personnel, including the Livermore Local Field Office (LFO).
Develop Work for Others (WFO's) proposals for the development of new security technologies.
Travel to DOE enterprise and industry partner sites in support of S&P projects, NA-70/713 discussions, DOE enterprise site visits, and industry partner meetings.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Additional Job Responsibilities, At The SEL.5 Level

Develop strategic initiatives to ensure the ongoing success of the whole enterprise consisting of seven (7) sites throughout the country, while creating a roadmap of future enterprise initiatives in collaboration with all stakeholders. Brief work to senior management on overall impact and approach.
Cultivate relationships with NNSA sponsors and technology leaders, while providing technical input and developing or refining new concepts in support of nuclear security priorities that promote LLNL skills, expertise, and technologies.
Cultivate and build relationships with other potential customers across the DOE, and Work for Others (WFO) (i.e., Department of Defense (DoD), and others) looking for additional program sponsors for new business opportunities.

Qualifications

This position requires an active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Nuclear Security or related discipline, or the equivalent combination of education and extensive related experience.
Significant experience solving complex system engineering problems in physical security systems or industrial control systems, intrusion detection systems, with in-depth experience in specialized areas.
Ability to motivate and collaborate effectively with other personnel in achieving project objectives.
Expert level experience leading complex programs and a proven record of resolving program management issues, as well as negotiating statements of work, timelines, and deliverables.
Expert level experience leading, tracking, and budgeting projects that require the application of creative innovation in managing and resource conflict resolution.
Ability to delegate effectively to accomplish goals within a multi-disciplinary team through leadership and positive influence, providing corrective measures when necessary.
Experience working with sponsors/government agencies, such as, NNSA, DOE, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), DOD, or other government agencies.
Expert communication, facilitation, and collaboration skills necessary to effectively present, explain, influence, and advise at all levels from staff to senior management.

Additional Qualifications At The SEL.5 Level

Expert knowledge of state-of-the-art technologies in physical security systems or industrial control systems.
Extensive experience successfully managing and leading multidisciplinary project teams with a successful history of producing high-quality cutting-edge technical products.
Extensive experience working with sponsors/government agencies, such as, NNSA, DOE, DHS DoD, or other government agencies.
Extensive experience developing and articulating strategic initiatives, and the ability to integrate and implement new programs and/or operational best practices.
Ability to champion, lead, and develop innovative cutting-edge technologies, theories, and concepts.

Pay Range

$227,430 - $346,140 Annually

$227,430 - $288,396 Annually for the SEL.4 level

$272,970 - $346,140 Annually for the SEL.5 level

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Additional Information

Position Information

This is a Career Indefinite position, open to Lab employees and external candidates.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
Flexible Benefits Package
401(k)
Relocation Assistance
Education Reimbursement Program
Flexible schedules (*depending on project needs)
Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

Security Clearance

This position requires an active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at time of hire.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How To Identify Fake Job Advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

To learn more about recruitment scams: https://www.llnl.gov/sites/www/files/2023-05/LLNL-Job-Fraud-Statement-Updated-4.26.23.pdf

Equal Employment Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer that is committed to providing all with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, protected veteran status, age, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Reasonable Accommodation

Our goal is to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates applying and interviewing at the Laboratory. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please use our online form to submit a request.

California Privacy Notice

The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) grants privacy rights to all California residents. The law also entitles job applicants, employees, and non-employee workers to be notified of what personal information LLNL collects and for what purpose. The Employee Privacy Notice can be accessed here.

Noblis is seeking a Geospatial Intelligence Analyst to work in a dynamic, mission-oriented environment within Bethesda, Maryland.

Geospatial Data Collection & Analysis: Gather, collate, and synthesize geospatial data from classified and unclassified sources; leverage tools and technologies to identify events, travel patterns, trends, pattern of life, and other intelligence of interest; conduct spatial and temporal analysis to detect anomalies, correlations, and patterns supporting intelligence requirements.
Intelligence Production & Reporting: Produce geospatial intelligence products — including annotated maps, overlays, assessments, and briefing materials — and deliver written and visual products that enable national-level decision-making.
Multi-Source Integration: Integrate geospatial analysis with other intelligence disciplines (SIGINT, HUMINT, OSINT) to deliver comprehensive, multi-source intelligence products.
Tool Proficiency & Development: Utilize and maintain proficiency in geospatial platforms such as ArcGIS, Google Earth, QGIS, and other mission-relevant applications; develop and refine workflows, processes, and methodologies to improve analytic efficiency and accuracy.
Emerging Technology Integration: Support the integration of emerging geospatial technologies and data sources into existing analytic workflows to enhance mission capabilities.
Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement: Coordinate with Intelligence Community (IC) partners, interagency stakeholders, and mission teams to define geospatial requirements, deliver tailored analytic support, and present findings and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership.

Required Qualifications

US Citizenship is required.
Must have an active Top Secret clearance with SCI access and CI Polygraph.
Bachelor’s degree with 4+ years of prior relevant experience OR a Master’s degree with 2+ years of prior relevant experience.
Proficiency with geospatial analysis tools and platforms (e.g., ArcGIS, Google Earth, RemoteView, or similar).
Experience gathering, collating, and synthesizing geospatial data from multiple sources to produce actionable intelligence.
Demonstrated ability to identify events, travel patterns, trends, and pattern of life through geospatial analysis.
Experience producing geospatial intelligence products, including maps, overlays, and geospatial assessments.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to integrate geospatial data with other intelligence disciplines.

Position Summary...

What you'll do...We are looking for someone who can step into an ambiguous business problem, ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, use data and AI to develop a point of view, and work with stakeholders to turn that insight into operational change.

Success in this role comes from critical thinking, structured problem solving, business judgment, analytical curiosity, and the ability to influence people. Data, technology, and AI are tools you will use to solve problems—not the end product.

You will work within Walmart Transportation, where relatively small improvements can operate at significant scale.

About the team:

Our team sits at the intersection of operations, analytics, technology, and transformation.

We work on problems where:

the question may not be clearly defined,
the data may not immediately tell the full story,
multiple stakeholders may see the problem differently,
and the solution often requires changing how work gets done.

Team members are expected to investigate, form hypotheses, use data to develop conviction, work directly with business partners, and help move ideas from analysis through implementation and measurement.

We value people who improve the thinking, not just execute the request they were given.

What you'll do:

Partner with operational stakeholders to understand problems, opportunities, and how work gets done.
Break ambiguous problems into clear questions and analytical approaches.
Use data to quantify opportunities, test hypotheses, and support business decisions.
Challenge assumptions when data or operational context suggests a different answer.
Identify patterns, inconsistencies, and root causes rather than stopping at surface-level reporting.
Translate analysis into clear recommendations business partners can understand and act on.
Influence stakeholders and drive adoption of changes without relying on positional authority.
Use AI and modern analytical tools to accelerate analysis, problem solving, and automation.
Validate and challenge AI-generated analysis, code, and recommendations before using them to make decisions.

What you'll bring:

We are looking for demonstrated evidence of the following: critical thinking, business/analytical judgment, ownership, stakeholder/change management, and technical/AI fluency.

You are comfortable working where the problem, answer, or process is not already defined.
You can interpret data, choose meaningful metrics, and distinguish useful signals from noise.
You take responsibility for the quality of the analysis and recommendation, regardless of which tools produced it.
You can communicate complex ideas clearly to nontechnical partners.

new_jobs.description:
Built's Mission:
Connect and simplify doing business in real estate.

Built is the AI-powered platform transforming the way real estate is financed, developed, and managed. Purpose-built for real estate and construction, Built began by fixing construction draw management for lenders and has grown into a comprehensive operating system addressing some of the industry’s most complex challenges. Today, Built is a partner to more than 350 lenders, over 80,000 borrowers and owners, and thousands of contractors, powering 86,000 active projects valued at more than $300 billion. Learn more at getbuilt.com
.

__________________________

Revenue Operations Analyst

About The Role

Built Technologies is transforming how capital moves through construction and real estate finance — one of the largest, most complex sectors in the economy. Our platform connects lenders, including many of the top U.S. banks, with the owners, developers, and general contractors they finance. When a draw is approved, a builder can pay subcontractors. When a compliance document clears, a project moves forward. The work we do here is not abstract — it has a direct and material impact on how capital flows and how real estate gets built.

Built's Revenue Operations team is the operational backbone of our entire revenue organization — managing the systems, data, and processes that enable Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Customer Support to operate with speed and precision.As a Revenue Operations Analyst, you will own key analytical and operational initiatives that provide data-driven insights to revenue leadership, translate CRM and business data into actionable insights, identify process gaps, and help drive greater consistency, efficiency, and alignment across the revenue organization.

As Revenue Operations evolves into an AI-native function, you will help rethink how our work gets done — using AI not simply to make existing tasks faster, but to redesign workflows, automate repetitive work, surface insights, and create more intelligent and scalable ways of operating. You will be expected to identify opportunities where AI can augment human decision-making, reduce manual effort, and improve the speed and quality of execution across the revenue organization.

You will operate with growing autonomy and produce work that leaders across the revenue organization rely on, while continuously looking for smarter, more scalable ways to solve problems and improve how RevOps operates.

Our Guiding Principles

Be Bold. We pursue the biggest problems in our industry, challenge assumptions others take for granted, and take calculated risks to get there. We don't hide behind consensus or committees. Playing it safe is just failing slowly.
Help Customers Win. We learn our customers' businesses deeply — how they think, how they deploy capital, what keeps them up at night. We treat their capital like our own. We ship leverage, not features. And we measure ourselves by customer results, not our intentions.
Move with Urgency & Purpose. We bias toward delivery over perfection, remove friction from our own paths, and communicate in real time. Momentum compounds — and we build it every day.
Own the Outcome. We own outcomes, not just tasks. We hold a high Say:Do ratio and take responsibility from idea through impact. When something breaks, we fix it — we don't wait to be asked.
Never Satisfied. We raise the bar continuously. We stay curious, hold exacting standards, debate hard, and hold our opinions loosely when the evidence shifts. Excellence is a habit, not an event.

What You'll Do

Keep the revenue engine running. Run the weekly pipeline review process in Salesforce. Identify stale opportunities, missing next steps, and changes to close dates or deal values that could affect the forecast; work with account owners to resolve them.Connect the customer lifecycle. Work across Marketing, Sales, Deal Desk, Finance, and Customer Success to coordinate handoffs from lead through closed-won, invoicing, expansion, and renewal. Make sure each team has the information and ownership needed to move forward. Help deals move cleanly from sale to revenue. Review closed-won deals for documented approvals, signed terms, products, lines of business, pricing types, and revenue assumptions. Resolve gaps before they create problems for forecasting, billing, or customer handoffs. Make the numbers trustworthy. Compare opportunities, deal documentation, billing inputs, and financial reports to identify missing or inconsistent revenue streams. Support invoice questions by checking billed amounts against contracts and amendments, and track discrepancies through resolution with Finance and account teams. Challenge what the reporting says. Review existing dashboards and recurring reports for sound definitions, accurate inputs, and results that reflect what is happening in the business. Use AI and other tools to test assumptions, investigate anomalies, and recommend changes to reporting logic. Improve forecast reliability. Maintain forecast inputs and compare projected bookings and revenue with actual results. Investigate differences, question the assumptions behind them, and work with stakeholders to improve future forecasts. Find and fix operational friction. Document recurring processes, clarify handoff ownership, and address the delays or errors that repeatedly slow down deals, billing, and reporting. Support smarter planning. Provide historical analysis and scenario support for territory, quota, and revenue planning. Make good processes easier to repeat. Use automation and approved AI tools to reduce manual work, catch exceptions earlier, and make recurring validation more efficient.

What You'll Bring

2–4+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Deal Desk, Finance Operations, or a related analytical and operational role — ideally within SaaS, fintech, or another complex B2B revenue environment where you have worked across the customer lifecycle from pipeline through closed-won, billing, expansion, and renewal.

An AI-native approach to operations. You are curious about how AI and automation can fundamentally improve how work gets done. You look beyond using AI to complete individual tasks faster and identify opportunities to redesign workflows, automate repetitive validation, surface exceptions earlier, and improve the speed and quality of decision-making.
A process-improvement mindset. You notice recurring friction, unclear ownership, manual work, and points where information breaks down across the revenue lifecycle. You can document the current process, identify the root cause, and recommend a more scalable way of operating.
Demonstrated ownership and cross-functional follow-through. You can independently manage recurring operational processes and analytical work, coordinate across Sales, Marketing, Deal Desk, Finance, and Customer Success, and proactively resolve gaps rather than simply identifying them.
Strong analytical judgment and attention to detail. You don't take a report or data point at face value. You question definitions and assumptions, investigate anomalies, validate information against source data, and distinguish between a reporting issue and something happening in the underlying business.
The ability to turn analysis into action. You can explain what the data is telling us, why it matters, and what should happen next. You communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders and follow issues through resolution.

What Success Looks Like At Six Months

You understand how the revenue lifecycle connects end to end. You can trace a customer from lead through closed-won, invoicing, expansion, and renewal; understand the critical data and ownership required at each stage; and recognize when a breakdown upstream will create problems downstream.
Revenue data is more trustworthy because of your work. You can reconcile information across Salesforce, deal documentation, billing inputs, and financial reporting, identify the source of discrepancies, and drive issues through resolution with Finance and account teams.
You are actively contributing to RevOps becoming an AI-native function. You have identified and implemented at least one meaningful use of AI or automation that goes beyond individual productivity — redesigning a recurring workflow, automating validation, surfacing exceptions earlier, or improving the speed and quality of operational decision-making.
You are operating with meaningful independence. You manage recurring RevOps responsibilities and analytical work with limited oversight, prioritize effectively, meet deadlines, and proactively surface risks, inconsistencies, and opportunities rather than waiting for someone to ask.
Cross-functional partners trust you to help solve problems, not just report them. Sales, Marketing, Deal Desk, Finance, and Customer Success increasingly rely on you to investigate issues, connect information across teams, clarify ownership, and help drive problems through resolution.

AI & Technology Expectations

Bring experience using Salesforce and Gong to manage pipeline, surface customer insights, and inform sales strategy.
Leverage AI tools to enhance the productivity, quality, and speed of your work.
Use AI to support drafting, analysis, summarization, and problem-solving across your role.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort through automation and AI.
Apply AI to sharpen decision-making and strengthen strategic insights.
Share effective AI use cases and best practices with your team.

Salary is just one component of Built's total compensation package for employees; your total rewards package at Built will include equity, market-current medical, dental and vision coverage, an unlimited PTO policy, and other benefits.

new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Analyst I or II (we are open to hiring at either level) to join the Statistics and Data Science department and support a diverse range of research projects. At NORC, Data Analysts are early career team members who train and work with our Statisticians and Data Scientists to perform tasks such as data processing, quality assurance, analysis, and dissemination.

As part of their data processing responsibilities, Data Analysts import, clean, standardize, transform, and validate data sets. They also research and document data procedures and support the investigation of data problems. They may identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns in data sets, support modeling efforts, and help prepare data presentations and reports, including developing charts, graphs, and tables. In addition, the Data Analyst may assist in data collection and harmonization from primary or secondary data sources (e.g., administrative records, commercial data, social media data), preparing data files for delivery, and the maintenance of databases, data systems, and their relevant metadata/dictionaries. The Data Analyst is expected to work collaboratively in a team environment.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location
: This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office.

DEPARTMENT: Statistics and Data Science

The Statistics and Data Science (SDS) department provides the scientific foundation required to advance NORC’s project portfolio. SDS delivers rigorous, innovative, and fit-for-purpose solutions along the project lifecycle. The department provides leadership for NORC’s approach on a broad range of approaches for study design and the analysis of primary and secondary data. SDS expertise includes artificial intelligence and machine learning; Bayesian analysis; causal inference; disclosure avoidance; imputation; data linkage and statistical matching for combining multiple data sources; data quality assessment; efficient and reproducible workflow development; privacy-preserving methods; small area estimation; statistical methods for survey sampling, weighting, estimation, and inference; and visualization.

The SDS department works closely with research, technology, and operational teams across NORC to ensure that statistical excellence and innovation remain central to the organization’s work. Many of NORC’s projects and proposals are led by substantive research departments that require significant contributions from SDS staff. SDS works closely with highly collaborative groups across the organization to ensure success through cross-departmental partnerships. To further capture the innovative spirit of NORC, SDS also leads projects that target departmental focus areas. Examples of recent project topics involving SDS staff include survey design, weighting, and analysis; AI for enhancing data quality, standardization, and integration; enhancing traffic safety data; linkage of health administrative data and surveys; and testing data visualization approaches for effective communication.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with statisticians, data scientists, technology experts, and subject matter experts to implement and improve data management and analysis activities.
Develop programs and scripts for data cleaning, integration, transformation, and harmonization, as well as data quality checks and validation
Support and enhance applications and databases already built for various research needs and produce data documentation and dictionaries.
Create data dashboards and visualizations, including preparing charts, graphs, and tables for reports and presentations.
Perform various types of data analysis and modeling, often involving multiple data sets.
Contribute to documentation, reports, and presentations through writing sections, creating basic analytic summaries, and developing tables and graphics.
Apply AI tools to help improve efficiency.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in statistics, data science, computer science, or an equivalent field.
0-2 years’ relevant experience (internships included).
Statistical programming in multiple packages and databases, including Python (required)
Familiarity working with large data sets, conducting statistical and quantitative modeling with strong programming.
Strong foundation in areas of analytic methods, data engineering, machine learning, and scientific methods of inquiry.
Experience with data management, data reduction techniques and data visualization.
Working knowledge of different types of data that can be sourced whether from administrative data, surveys, social media, or sensor data.
Strong skills in problem solving and quantitative analysis are required, including a willingness to understand deviations and ask questions about data issues.
Able to organize and prioritize work assignments to meet project needs.
Strong communication, writing and data storytelling skills.
Enthusiasm for teamwork and collaboration across disciplinary boundaries.

Preferred Skills

Preferred Skills:

Experience working with SAS, Tableau, Hadoop, Hive, Databricks, MapReduce, and/or other large data systems
Additional expertise in large and small language models, and machine learning, in working in cloud environments (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), and with command-line workflows (e.g., in bash)
Experience with JavaScript programming.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. now and in the future. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.

Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $62,000-$73,000.

Benefits

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment
Dental and vision insurance
